74298007.title: Licensing, Security & Management: Making Microsoft 365 Defender and Intune Work Together with Videsh Chavan
74298007.key: licensing security management making microsoft 365 defender and intune work together with videsh chavan
74298007.markup: {{link|https://www.m365.fm/microsoft-365-licensing/|Microsoft 365 licensing}} is often treated as a procurement problem: choose E3, E5, E7 or a collection of add-ons, assign the licenses, and move on. But licensing decisions directly influence security architecture, endpoint management, identity protection, and operational costs. In {{link|https://www.m365.fm/videsh-chavan/|this episode}} of M365 FM, Mirko Peters talks with Videsh Chavan about building a unified {{link|https://www.m365.fm/categories/power-platform-talk/|Microsoft 365}} strategy where licensing, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, identity, and endpoint security work together instead of operating as separate silos. ㅤ MICROSOFT 365 LICENSING IS AN ARCHITECTURE DECISION One of the central ideas of the conversation is that Microsoft 365 licensing shouldn't be treated purely as procurement. Organizations frequently purchase licenses without mapping the capabilities those licenses actually unlock. The result can be expensive features that nobody uses, duplicated security products, and security gaps that only become visible after an incident. Videsh recommends looking at licensing, Intune, Defender, and identity as parts of one connected architecture. Organizations should understand which capabilities they own, which capabilities they actually use, and where third-party products duplicate functionality already included in Microsoft licensing. ㅤ A FIVE-STEP MICROSOFT 365 SECURITY FRAMEWORK The discussion introduces a practical five-step approach for moving from disconnected Microsoft 365 tools toward a unified strategy. It starts with a licensing audit and capability mapping, followed by establishing an identity-first security baseline. Intune then becomes the enforcement layer, while Defender serves as the detection and response layer. The final component is continuous cost and coverage review, ensuring that licensing, security controls, and actual organizational requirements remain aligned. ㅤ IDENTITY AS THE FOUNDATION OF MODERN SECURITY As employees work from offices, homes, personal devices, mobile platforms, and Cloud PCs, the traditional corporate network becomes less useful as the primary security boundary. Identity therefore becomes a critical foundation. Users, groups, applications, connectors, access controls, and other resources depend heavily on identity. The conversation explores why organizations need strong identity controls, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/conditional-access-simply-explained/|Conditional Access}}, MFA, and appropriate security guardrails as part of their Microsoft 365 architecture. ㅤ AUDIT WHAT YOU ACTUALLY OWN Before purchasing additional Microsoft security products, organizations should understand their existing entitlements. Videsh recommends inventorying assigned versus actively used licenses and mapping license tiers such as E3 and E5 against the Intune, Defender, identity, and security capabilities they unlock. This can expose features the organization already pays for but doesn't use. Regular reviews can also identify unused add-ons, capability gaps, and situations where upgrading or downgrading particular users makes more sense than applying the same licensing tier to everybody. ㅤ WHY INTUNE IS MORE THAN MDM Microsoft Intune has evolved far beyond traditional mobile device management. In the architecture discussed in this episode, Intune acts as an enforcement layer covering device configuration, application management, security policies, patching, provisioning, and endpoint security. Rather than maintaining large numbers of disconnected policies, organizations should consider structured security baselines and manageable policy architectures. The objective is to make endpoint management easier to understand, maintain, and continuously improve. ㅤ {{link|https://www.m365.fm/windows-autopilot/|WINDOWS AUTOPILOT}} AND ZERO-TOUCH PROVISIONING Windows Autopilot fundamentally changes traditional corporate device provisioning. Instead of IT departments manually building and imaging every laptop before handing it to an employee, devices can be shipped directly from suppliers to users. The employee can unpack the device, connect it to the internet, authenticate, and allow organizational policies and configurations to provision the endpoint. This approach became particularly valuable as remote and hybrid work increased and organizations needed to onboard employees without requiring them to physically visit an office. ㅤ INTUNE AS A SECURITY ENFORCEMENT LAYER Intune increasingly sits at the intersection of endpoint management and cybersecurity. Security baselines, antivirus configurations, application policies, device configurations, and other endpoint controls can be centrally managed and enforced. This makes Intune an important part of the broader Microsoft security architecture rather than simply a tool for configuring laptops and smartphones. ㅤ MICROSOFT DEFENDER AS DETECTION AND RESPONSE Microsoft Defender represents a broader family of security capabilities rather than a single antivirus product. Organizations need to understand which Defender capabilities their licenses provide and how those capabilities fit into the wider endpoint security architecture. The episode discusses a practical security loop: detect suspicious activity, evaluate what happened, restrict the affected device or access when necessary, and restore normal operations after the problem has been addressed. Security teams remain responsible for investigating alerts and determining whether activity represents a genuine threat or a false positive. ㅤ ZERO TRUST IS A STRATEGY, NOT A PRODUCT Zero Trust isn't another Microsoft product organizations can simply purchase and enable. It is a cybersecurity strategy built around continuously verifying access instead of automatically trusting users, devices, or connections. Identity verification, application context, security controls, and least-privilege access all contribute to this model. Zero Trust therefore needs to influence architectural decisions across the organization rather than becoming another isolated security project. ㅤ AI AND THE FUTURE OF ENDPOINT MANAGEMENT AI introduces another layer to modern endpoint operations. Instead of waiting until users report that their device has a problem, telemetry and AI-assisted analysis can potentially identify deteriorating device health, recurring crashes, or other problems earlier. This creates an opportunity for more predictive and proactive IT operations. Videsh doesn't suggest handing endpoint management entirely to AI, but sees opportunities to shift some repetitive Level 1 activities toward AI-assisted operations while people remain responsible for more complex decisions. ㅤ MODERNIZING A LARGE ENTERPRISE For an enterprise operating Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, Windows 365, Active Directory, existing SCCM infrastructure, thousands of applications, BYOD, multiple Microsoft licensing tiers, and third-party security products, modernization should begin with discovery. Organizations need to understand their users, business requirements, existing technologies, licensing, regional restrictions, security requirements, and future use cases before redesigning the architecture. Modernization should then be controlled through documentation, peer review, architecture standards, and carefully managed implementation to minimize disruption. ㅤ THE KEY TAKEAWAY Microsoft 365 licensing, Intune, Defender, identity, Conditional Access, device health, and security policies shouldn't be managed as unrelated technologies. Together, they form a connected architecture in which identity and device signals influence access while Intune enforces policies and Defender provides detection and response. The starting point is understanding what the organization already owns and how those capabilities are being used. From there, organizations can identify security gaps, eliminate unnecessary licensing duplication, modernize endpoint management, and build a more coherent Microsoft 365 security strategy. As Mirko summarizes at the end of the conversation: licensing isn't simply procurement, Intune isn't simply device management, Defender isn't simply antivirus, and identity isn't simply a username and password. 74287285.title: Dynamics 365 Agents - Simply Explained
74287285.markup: Dynamics 365 Agents take AI beyond answering questions and generating drafts. Instead of waiting for someone to ask {{link|https://www.m365.fm/categories/copilot-talk/|https://www.m365.fm/categories/copilot-talk/}} for help, agents can respond to defined business events, work with approved Dynamics 365 data, follow predefined rules, take permitted actions, and hand work to people when human judgment is required. In {{link|https://www.m365.fm/dynamics-365-agents-simply-explained/|https://www.m365.fm/dynamics-365-agents-simply-explained/}} of M365 FM, Mirko Peters explains how Dynamics 365 Agents work across sales, customer service, finance, supply chain, Business Central, Field Service, and Project Operations — and why permissions, guardrails, data quality, and human oversight are critical. ㅤ WHAT ARE DYNAMICS 365 AGENTS? ㅤ A Dynamics 365 Agent is AI configured to watch for a business event, understand approved information, follow defined rules, perform permitted actions, and report what happened. The important difference is that an agent doesn't simply wait for a user to ask a question. A trigger such as a new lead, customer email, supplier response, order request, or financial mismatch can start the process automatically. ㅤ COPILOT VS DYNAMICS 365 AGENTS ㅤ Copilot typically works beside the user. You open a customer case and ask for a summary, request information, or generate a draft. The interaction begins because you asked Copilot to help. An agent can continue working in the background according to its defined job. It can monitor an approved process, identify an event, collect relevant information, perform allowed actions, and escalate the work when necessary. Think of Copilot as an assistant sitting beside you, while an agent is a specialized team member with a narrow job description, specific permissions, and clear rules. ㅤ HOW THE AI AGENT LOOP WORKS ㅤ The basic agent process can be understood as: notice, understand, act, check, and hand over. The agent notices a defined event such as a new message or lead. It understands the situation using information and rules it has permission to access. It performs allowed actions, checks whether the result remains within its boundaries, and hands the work to a person when judgment or approval is required. This creates supervised automation rather than unrestricted AI autonomy. ㅤ GUARDRAILS, PERMISSIONS AND HUMAN CONTROL ㅤ Guardrails define what an agent can see, change, create, or send. An organization might allow an agent to create a draft email but prevent it from sending that message automatically. An agent could categorize a customer case but be prevented from issuing a refund. The same principle applies to supplier communication, financial transactions, customer promises, contracts, and other sensitive activities. The agent can prepare and route the work while people retain responsibility for higher-risk decisions. ㅤ DATAVERSE AND COPILOT STUDIO ㅤ Many Dynamics 365 applications use Microsoft Dataverse as the connected data foundation for customers, contacts, leads, cases, activities, products, and other business information. For custom agents, Copilot Studio provides a place where organizations can define instructions, connect approved knowledge sources, configure actions, and determine how an agent should respond. The quality of these agents depends heavily on the quality of the underlying data and processes. ㅤ SALES QUALIFICATION AGENTS ㅤ Sales agents can help close the gap between incoming interest and seller follow-up. A Sales Qualification Agent can research incoming leads, compare them against criteria established by the sales organization, prioritize potential opportunities, and prepare personalized outreach. Instead of sellers spending significant time performing the first round of research for every new lead, the agent can prepare information while the salesperson decides whether the prospect deserves further attention. ㅤ SALES RESEARCH AND OPPORTUNITY AGENTS ㅤ Sales Research Agents can gather approved information before customer conversations, helping sellers understand companies, previous interactions, existing opportunities, and relevant account context. Opportunity Agents operate later in the sales process. They can research active opportunities, surface deal context, identify potential risks, and highlight opportunities requiring attention. Sales Close Agents can support the final stages through follow-ups, customer engagement, product suggestions, and handling common objections within defined business rules. ㅤ CUSTOMER SERVICE AGENTS ㅤ {{link|https://www.m365.fm/dynamics-365-customer-service-simply-explained/|https://www.m365.fm/dynamics-365-customer-service-simply-explained/}} Agents can reduce repetitive administrative work around customer cases. A Case Management Agent can interpret incoming customer communications, create cases, extract useful details, associate customers, and route cases appropriately. Customer Intent Agents can identify why customers are contacting the organization and help direct requests toward appropriate queues, answers, or service representatives. This can reduce the time agents spend manually creating and categorizing cases before they can begin solving the customer's actual problem. ㅤ KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT AND QUALITY AGENTS ㅤ A Customer Knowledge Management Agent can analyze completed cases to identify gaps in an organization's knowledge base and help prepare draft knowledge articles for human review. Quality Evaluation Agents can evaluate larger numbers of customer interactions against standards established by service supervisors. This can help managers identify patterns and coaching opportunities without depending entirely on manually selected samples. ㅤ BUSINESS CENTRAL SALES ORDER AGENTS ㅤ In Dynamics 365 Business Central, a Sales Order Agent can process incoming customer order requests. It can read an order request received through email, identify the customer, extract requested products and quantities, and prepare order information for review. People remain responsible for exceptions such as unusual pricing, missing products, incorrect customer information, or orders that don't match established patterns. ㅤ SUPPLY CHAIN AND SUPPLIER AGENTS ㅤ The Supplier Communications Agent in {{link|https://www.m365.fm/dynamics-365-supply-chain-management/|https://www.m365.fm/dynamics-365-supply-chain-management/}} can support repetitive supplier follow-up activities. It can request purchase order confirmations, ask suppliers for delivery updates, process incoming supplier communications, and associate responses with relevant orders. If a supplier reports a significant delay or another situation requiring a business decision, the agent can escalate the issue to a buyer or planner. ㅤ FINANCE AND RECONCILIATION AGENTS ㅤ Finance agents can support repetitive reconciliation work. An Account Reconciliation Agent can compare transactions and identify records that should match but don't, helping finance teams discover discrepancies earlier. Financial Reconciliation Agents can support preparation and cleanup of information required for reconciliation and financial reporting. Accountants still determine what discrepancies mean and approve the appropriate resolution. ㅤ FIELD SERVICE AND PROJECT OPERATIONS AGENTS ㅤ {{link|https://www.m365.fm/dynamics-365-field-service/|https://www.m365.fm/dynamics-365-field-service/}} can use scheduling-focused agents to help optimize technician schedules when appointments, availability, priorities, or other conditions change. Project Operations can use agents to support administrative activities such as preparing time entries, processing expense information, and reviewing time, expense, and material records against organizational policies. These capabilities target repetitive administrative work while keeping people responsible for exceptions and consequential decisions. ㅤ WHY DATA QUALITY MATTERS ㅤ An AI agent can only work with the information available to it. Duplicate customers, incomplete product records, outdated supplier contacts, and inconsistent business data can quickly reduce the reliability of automated processes. Automation doesn't transform poor data into good decisions. Organizations need clean and consistent records before expecting agents to reliably connect incoming information with the correct customers, orders, cases, or suppliers. ㅤ HOW TO START WITH DYNAMICS 365 AGENTS ㅤ Start with one repetitive process that has clear steps, clear ownership, and a measurable result. Define what triggers the process, which records the agent can access, which actions it can perform, which actions require approval, and exactly when the agent must stop and involve a person. Testing should include normal situations as well as difficult exceptions. Organizations should inspect what the agent reads, prepares, changes, and escalates before expanding its permissions or applying the approach to additional processes. ㅤ THE KEY TAKEAWAY ㅤ Dynamics 365 Agents turn repetitive business processes into supervised AI-powered actions. They can respond to events, understand approved business information, execute defined tasks, and escalate exceptions across sales, customer service, finance, operations, supply chain, and project workflows. The objective isn't to give AI control of an entire department. Start with one clearly defined queue or process, establish permissions and guardrails, measure the result, and expand only after the process proves reliable. An agent can only perform as well as the process, data, rules, and boundaries you give it. 74187792.title: AI Turns Integration into an Organism as a Service — How Azure Logic Apps Are Changing Enterprise Integration with Sonny Gillissen [MVP]
74187792.key: ai turns integration into an organism as a service how azure logic apps are changing enterprise integration with sonny gillissen mvp
74187792.markup:
Enterprise integration is usually invisible until it breaks, and deterministic workflows struggle with the unexpected. This episode is for architects and integration developers who want to understand Azure Logic Apps, connectors, identity and observability, and how agent loops can make integrations adaptive and self-healing. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Intro: integration as a commodity
- 02:05 – Sonny's path into integration and why enterprise integration gets complex
- 07:29 – What Azure Integration Services include
- 11:29 – Logic Apps, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, consumption vs. standard
- 20:38 – The connector ecosystem and its security trade-offs
- 27:11 – Authentication, managed identities and least privilege
- 30:59 – Observability, tracked properties and business-driven logging
- 49:37 – Organism as a Service: agent loops and self-healing integrations

**Key takeaways**
- Azure Integration Services combine Logic Apps, API Management, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-functions/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=ai-turns-integration-into-an-organism-as-a-service|Azure Functions}}, Service Bus and Event Grid, and the right mix depends on whether a team prefers low code or pro code.
- Secure integrations rely on built-in connectors where possible, managed identities, Key Vault and least-privilege permissions so that one breached connection cannot take down every integration.
- With agent loops in Logic Apps, integrations can interpret errors and intent and react to unexpected situations, turning integration as a service into what Sonny Gillissen calls Organism as a Service.

**Worth quoting** “And in an Azure logic app, it's just a canvas. So as soon as you run your first logic app, you can see what it did, why it did it, what's the result?” – Sonny Gillissen (12:34) “Our main objective is to always use built-in connectors when you can, because the built-in connectors are running within the logic app runtime.” – Sonny Gillissen (26:17) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/sonny-gillissen/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=ai-turns-integration-into-an-organism-as-a-service|Episode page}}: the full conversation with chapters, quotes and FAQ on Azure Logic Apps

74176895.title: Dynamics 365 Unified Routing - Simply Explained
74176895.markup:
Growing service teams quickly find that one shared queue sends urgent cases to the wrong people or leaves them waiting. This episode explains Dynamics 365 unified routing for customer service leads and admins. You learn how workstreams, queues, skills and capacity work together so every request reaches the right agent the first time. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Requests stuck in a shared queue
- 00:33 – Why basic queues stop working
- 03:00 – Classification and assignment
- 06:50 – Workstreams, queues, skills and capacity
- 11:23 – One request from message to agent
- 14:49 – Planning a routing model
- 17:37 – Conclusion

**Key takeaways**
- Unified routing first classifies incoming work with skills, language and priority, then assigns it to an available agent who has the right skills and free capacity.
- Workstreams define the path for each kind of work, queues set team ownership, skills describe fit, and capacity profiles plus presence show who can take work now.
- Build queues, people, skills and capacity before routing rules, keep rules minimal, and give the fallback queue an owner who watches it.

**Worth quoting** “A queue only answers part of the question, it can tell you where a request should wait, but it doesn't always decide which available person has the right knowledge, who already handles several chats, or whether a more urgent request should come first.” – Mirko Peters (01:34) “Your service leaders still decide which customers need faster help, what skills matter, how many chats an agent can manage, and where work should go when nobody matches. Unified routing takes those decisions and applies them the same way each time.” – Mirko Peters (02:36) **Explore more on M365.FM**

74133476.title: Dynamics 365 Project Operations - Simply Explained
74133476.markup: Customer projects can become complicated quickly. Sales has the customer relationship and quote. Project managers have schedules and tasks. Resource managers need to know who is available. Consultants record hours and expenses. Finance needs to understand costs, revenue, and what can actually be invoiced.In {{link|https://www.m365.fm/dynamics-365-project-operations-simply-explained/|this episode}} of Microsoft Knowledge Nuggets on M365 FM, Mirko Peters explains Microsoft {{link|https://www.m365.fm/categories/power-platform-talk/|Dynamics 365}} Project Operations and how Microsoft connects project sales, project management, resource planning, time tracking, expenses, billing, and financial processes within one project-focused platform.The episode follows the complete lifecycle of a customer project—from the first sales conversation and project quote through planning, staffing, delivery, time and expense management, financial tracking, and finally customer invoicing. WHAT IS DYNAMICS 365 PROJECT OPERATIONS? Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations is designed for organizations that sell project-based services. These businesses are not simply selling products. They are selling expertise, professional services, consulting hours, engineering work, implementation projects, design services, development work, or other customer engagements where people, time, costs, contracts, and billing need to remain connected.Without a connected system, different departments often create their own version of a project. Sales knows what was promised. Delivery creates another project plan. Employees record hours somewhere else. Finance receives approved hours and expenses later and then tries to determine what should appear on the customer's invoice.Dynamics 365 Project Operations connects these areas around shared project information.The objective is not to make every department use exactly the same interface. Salespeople, consultants, project managers, resource managers, and finance professionals have different responsibilities. What matters is that the underlying project information remains connected. FROM SALES OPPORTUNITY TO PROJECT DELIVERY A customer project begins before the first task is created.During the sales process, someone needs to determine what the customer actually needs, which roles will be required, how many hours may be necessary, when work could start, what the project should cost, and how the customer will be charged.Dynamics 365 Project Operations helps organizations capture this information while the opportunity is still being developed.This creates an important connection between what sales promises and what the delivery organization eventually needs to provide.Instead of project managers receiving an email saying that sales has apparently sold several weeks of consulting, the approved scope, roles, estimated effort, pricing, dates, and billing conditions can become part of the connected project record. PROJECT QUOTES AND CONTRACTS Quotes and project contracts establish the commercial foundation of a customer engagement.A quote represents what the organization proposes to sell. It can include planned work, estimated effort, project roles, pricing, expected dates, and billing conditions.Once the customer accepts the proposal, the project contract records what the customer actually agreed to purchase.This distinction is important because delivery teams should work against the accepted customer commitment rather than an earlier version of the proposal that may have changed during negotiations.Contracts can also establish whether customers are charged according to time worked, a fixed project price, milestones, or other agreed billing arrangements. PROJECT PLANNING AND WORK BREAKDOWN STRUCTURES After the customer accepts the project, the promise needs to become an executable plan.Project managers break large outcomes into smaller pieces of work. This structure is commonly called a Work Breakdown Structure, or WBS.For example, a cloud migration project might contain discovery, design, implementation, testing, customer review, deployment, and closure phases.Each part can then contain individual tasks with planned dates, expected effort, responsibilities, and dependencies.Dependencies are particularly important because project activities rarely happen completely independently. Design may depend on discovery. Testing depends on implementation. Customer approval may depend on testing.When one activity changes, project managers need visibility into what that change could mean for the rest of the schedule. PROJECT MILESTONES Milestones provide recognizable checkpoints during a project.A milestone might represent design approval, completion of testing, delivery of a major project component, customer acceptance, or another significant event.Unlike normal tasks, milestones typically represent a point in the project rather than a block of working hours.They are useful for communicating progress and can also have commercial importance. In milestone-based engagements, reaching an agreed milestone may trigger part of the customer's billing schedule.This connects project delivery directly with the commercial agreement. PROJECT TIME TRACKING Time entries are more than administrative timesheets.When employees record time against specific projects and tasks, the organization gains information about how much effort the work actually requires.Project managers can compare planned effort with actual effort. If discovery was expected to require 40 hours but has already consumed 60 hours, that difference becomes visible while the project is still active.That does not automatically mean the project is failing. The customer environment may simply have been more complicated than expected.The important point is that the organization now has information it can act on rather than discovering the problem after the project has finished.Approved time can also become an important input into project costs and customer billing. PROJECT EXPENSE MANAGEMENT Customer projects frequently involve costs beyond employee time.Consultants may travel to customer locations, purchase approved services, or incur other project-related expenses.Dynamics 365 Project Operations can associate these expenses with the relevant customer project instead of allowing them to disappear into disconnected receipts, emails, or financial records.This creates better visibility for project managers and provides finance with clearer information when reviewing project profitability and customer billing. RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND STAFFING A perfect project plan is useless if the required people are unavailable.Resource management connects project requirements with employees and contractors who have the appropriate skills and availability.A project manager may know that a security specialist is required for two weeks without initially knowing which individual will perform the work.Resource management allows organizations to consider both requirements.Someone may have exactly the right technical skills but already be assigned to another customer. Another person might have the necessary expertise and sufficient capacity during the required period.This helps organizations reduce overbooking and make project commitments based on actual resource availability. RESOURCE BOOKINGS AND CAPACITY A resource booking reserves part of someone's working capacity for project work.Employees do not necessarily need to be assigned full-time. A consultant might spend three days each week on one customer project while using the remaining capacity for another engagement, training, internal work, or leave.Connecting resource bookings with availability gives organizations a clearer picture of their delivery capacity.This is particularly valuable for consulting organizations and professional services firms where people represent both the primary delivery resource and a significant part of project cost. SKILLS, ROLES AND PROJECT COSTS Staffing is not simply about finding someone with an empty calendar.Projects often require specific roles and competencies such as project managers, business analysts, developers, architects, engineers, consultants, or security specialists.The financial impact also matters.A senior specialist may have a different internal cost than a junior consultant. The organization therefore needs to balance skills, availability, delivery quality, and financial performance when staffing projects.Dynamics 365 Project Operations connects these staffing decisions more closely with the overall project plan and financial picture. PROJECT COSTS AND PROFITABILITY A project can finish on time and still lose money.Customer revenue represents only one side of the financial equation. Organizations also need to consider employee costs, contractors, travel, software, materials, and other expenses required to deliver the engagement.Dynamics 365 Project Operations helps connect planned and actual project costs with customer pricing.This makes it easier to understand whether the project is consuming more expensive resources or more working hours than originally anticipated.A project can therefore appear successful operationally while becoming less profitable financially.Connecting project delivery and project financial information helps organizations identify this situation earlier. 74111862.title: From Garage Band to Symphony Orchestra- How Microsoft 365 Governance Creates Harmony at Scale — with Heiko Brenn
74111862.key: from garage band to symphony orchestra how microsoft 365 governance creates harmony at scale with heiko brenn
74111862.markup:
As Microsoft 365 grows, Teams, SharePoint sites and guest accounts multiply until collaboration turns into noise. In this interview, Heiko Brenn of BCC uses music metaphors to show IT leaders and governance owners how ownership, lifecycle management, monitoring and automation turn that sprawl into a well-coordinated orchestra. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – From garage band to orchestra: the governance challenge
- 02:28 – Heiko Brenn's journey from Exchange 5.5 to BCC
- 05:18 – What Microsoft 365 governance means
- 10:16 – Governance is a team sport
- 14:26 – Music metaphors: bands, conductors and jam sessions
- 28:58 – AI as conductor, workload rules and the sound check
- 35:54 – Governance maturity and detecting drift
- 45:43 – Sprawl, BCC's role and rapid-fire round

**Key takeaways**
- Microsoft 365 governance is the balance between creativity, freedom and structure, and it works best in the background so people can collaborate without bureaucracy getting in the way.
- Governance is a team sport that needs a leadership sponsor, IT and security, and line-of-business owners, with different rules for areas such as HR and legal than for sales or marketing.
- Start early with basic policies such as naming conventions, ownership and lifecycle rules for Teams and guests, then monitor for drift and automate so sprawl stays under control as the organization grows.

**Worth quoting** “So from my perspective, I would say governance in general is a team sport. So it's really about involving all the different, I would say even everything that you mentioned is part of the process.” – Heiko Brenn (10:33) “So I would definitely start at an early stage with some maybe more simplified rules, but have something in place already.” – Heiko Brenn (22:19) **Explore more on M365.FM**

74081090.title: Microsoft Purview Data Map - Simply Explained
74081090.key: microsoft purview data map simply explained
74081090.markup:
Data rarely stays in one app: it is copied, exported, renamed and forgotten across Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and Fabric. This episode is for Microsoft 365 admins, data owners and compliance teams who need a plain-English map of Microsoft Purview. You learn how its data map, catalog, labels, DLP and investigation tools fit together to make data findable, trustworthy and protected. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why data sprawl turns into business risk
- 04:39 – What Microsoft Purview actually is
- 08:44 – Find, name and trust data: data map, catalog and lineage
- 12:13 – Classify and protect: sensitivity labels and DLP
- 16:18 – Manage risk, records and investigations
- 19:47 – How the pieces work together

**Key takeaways**
- Microsoft Purview does not store your data; it adds rules, context and visibility around data that stays in Microsoft 365, Azure, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/fabric/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-purview-data-map-simply-explained|Fabric}} and supported external sources.
- The data map, unified catalog, glossary, lineage and data quality checks help people find data, know who owns it and judge whether it can be trusted.
- Sensitivity labels, DLP, audit, retention, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/ediscovery/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-purview-data-map-simply-explained|eDiscovery}} and communication compliance protect information as it moves and give responsible teams records and context when something goes wrong.

**Worth quoting** “An accessible report is not always a trusted report. That difference can save a team from building a decision around incomplete or outdated information.” – Mirko Peters (12:09) “A sensitivity label and DLP work together, but they do different jobs. The label identifies information and describes how it should be handled. DLP checks an action as it happens and can warn the person, block the action or record it for review.” – Mirko Peters (14:43) **Explore more on M365.FM**

74080233.title: Microsoft Entra Connect - Simply Explained
74080233.markup:
Duplicate accounts, separate passwords and leavers who keep cloud access are classic hybrid identity problems. This episode explains Microsoft Entra Connect in plain English for IT admins and anyone running Active Directory alongside Microsoft 365. You will learn how sync, authentication and health monitoring work together and where the tool's limits are. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Two identity systems, one person
- 01:06 – Active Directory and Entra ID
- 04:41 – Building block one: Sync
- 08:48 – Building block two: Authentication
- 13:38 – Building block three: Health
- 15:44 – What Entra Connect does not do
- 18:25 – One employee, one connected identity
- 19:20 – Put it to work

**Key takeaways**
- Microsoft Entra Connect is the controlled bridge that syncs selected users, groups and details from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID, with Active Directory remaining the source of authority.
- Password hash synchronization fits most organizations, pass-through authentication keeps the local directory in every password check, and federation suits existing sign-in systems.
- Entra Connect Health warns when sync stops, which matters most when disabled accounts must also lose cloud access, and Entra Connect is neither a backup nor a replacement for MFA or {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/conditional-access/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-connect|conditional access}}.

**Worth quoting** “Editing the same synced detail directly in EntraID can either fail or get replaced later by the local value. That sounds strict, but it prevents two filing cabinets from arguing over which record is correct.” – Mirko Peters (04:14) “But sync has a clear limit. Entra Connect doesn't assign a Microsoft 365 license, just because it creates Alex's cloud account. It also doesn't create a mailbox by itself.” – Mirko Peters (07:28) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/microsoft-entra-connect/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-connect|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, quotes and an FAQ on hybrid identity
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-connect/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-connect|Microsoft Entra Connect}} – the bridge this episode explains, covering sync, sign-in methods, health monitoring and its limits
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/active-directory/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-connect|Active Directory}} – the on-premises staff directory that stays the source of authority for synced users
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-connect|Microsoft Entra ID}} – the cloud directory that receives synced identities and handles Microsoft 365 sign-ins and access

74079342.title: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync - Simply Explained
74079342.key: microsoft entra cloud sync simply explained
74079342.markup:
Many organizations still keep identities in on-premises Active Directory while their people work in Microsoft 365. This knowledge nugget helps identity admins understand Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync, how it differs from Entra Connect, what changed in 2026, and how to run a safe, small pilot before deciding. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Intro: two places where identity matters
- 00:52 – Why identity sync exists
- 03:55 – What Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync actually is
- 07:57 – High availability and multiple forests
- 11:00 – Scoping, mappings, provision on demand and safeguards
- 14:39 – Cloud Sync versus Entra Connect and the 2026 shift
- 18:22 – A safe first move for your company

**Key takeaways**
- Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync moves most identity sync processing into Microsoft Entra, leaving only lightweight provisioning agents in the local network that connect outbound to the cloud.
- Multiple agents provide built-in failover and can connect separate Active Directory forests to one tenant, while scoping by OU or security group and provision on demand keep pilots controlled.
- Entra Connect still fits setups with pass-through authentication, federation, advanced custom rules or specific {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/exchange-online/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-cloud-sync-simply-explained|Exchange}} hybrid needs, so compare requirements before migrating and never let both tools manage the same objects.

**Worth quoting** “No, Cloud sync is newer but newer does not automatically mean it fits your setup. The right choice depends on what your identity system needs to do today, not on which product sounds more modern.” – Mirko Peters (14:45) “An outbound connection means the agent starts the conversation with the cloud. You don't need to open your network and wait for an unknown connection to come in.” – Mirko Peters (04:30) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/microsoft-entra-cloud-sync/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-cloud-sync-simply-explained|Episode page}}: the full knowledge nugget with chapters, quotes and FAQ
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-cloud-sync/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-cloud-sync-simply-explained|Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync}} – the main topic, covering lightweight agents, cloud-managed configuration, scoping and the 2026 additions

- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/active-directory/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-cloud-sync-simply-explained|Active Directory}} – the on-premises source of user records that Cloud Sync reads and keeps authoritative

Everyone wants Copilot and agents, but fragmented data and weak governance undermine trustworthy answers. Mirko Peters talks with Walter Calcagno about Microsoft Fabric, semantic models, ontology layers, metadata and his AI readiness approach. Data architects, BI teams and decision makers learn what must exist between the lakehouse and a reliable AI experience. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Intro: is your data ready for {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-fabric-architecture-data-ready-copilot-walter-calcagno|Copilot}}?
- 02:47 – Walter's path from accounting to data and Spanish content
- 09:34 – Power BI and asking the right business questions
- 19:09 – Microsoft Fabric, OneLake and Delta Lake
- 24:25 – Semantic models, ontology and AI access
- 30:20 – Medallion layers and data ready for AI
- 37:39 – AI readiness assessment and the seven-layer model
- 48:07 – {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/governance/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-fabric-architecture-data-ready-copilot-walter-calcagno|Governance}}, Fabric Apps and rapid fire

**Key takeaways**
- AI on enterprise data starts with business questions, clear KPI definitions and governance, not with a chat prompt or a specific tool.
- In Microsoft Fabric, semantic models and an ontology layer above them give LLMs a governed, cost-efficient path to the right data, guided by good metadata.
- Medallion architecture is flexible: use as many layers as needed, at least two, and prepare specific data for AI to keep token costs under control.

**Worth quoting** “So companies don't need to make more dashboard. They need to answer more business question because the real business is on the street” – Walter Calcagno (16:55) “You need to define what is your definition of the KPI. If you have sales in your perspective, you need to prompt that into the LLM.” – Walter Calcagno (36:40) **Explore more on M365.FM**

74004180.title: Microsoft Entra Domain Services - Simply Explained
74004180.key: microsoft entra domain services simply explained
74004180.markup:
Moving an old Windows app to an Azure VM does not remove its need for a classic domain with LDAP, Kerberos and Group Policy. This Knowledge Nugget shows IT admins and cloud architects where Microsoft Entra Domain Services fits next to Entra ID and Active Directory, and which limits to check before choosing it. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The cloud app that still expects a Windows domain
- 00:45 – Why Entra ID alone cannot run every legacy app
- 03:28 – What Microsoft Entra Domain Services actually is
- 07:20 – Entra ID, Active Directory and Domain Services: different jobs
- 10:40 – When Domain Services fits and when it does not
- 13:53 – The managed-service trade-offs
- 15:35 – A simple Azure migration story

**Key takeaways**
- Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides a managed Windows domain inside an Azure virtual network for legacy apps that still need LDAP, Kerberos, NTLM, domain join or Group Policy, without you running domain controllers.
- Identity data flows one way, from on-premises Active Directory or Entra ID into the managed domain, so users and groups must be managed in the source directory, and cloud-only users may need a password change before they can use it.
- New cloud apps should sign in directly through Entra ID; Domain Services does not fit apps that need LDAP write access, schema changes or full domain admin control.

**Worth quoting** “The main identity record stays in Entra ID. Users and groups from Entra ID copy into the managed domain so the older app can see and use them in the form it understands.” – Mirko Peters (05:16) “For cloud-only users, that often means the user needs to change their password after domain services is enabled. That password change creates the protected form needed for the managed domain.” – Mirko Peters (06:18) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/microsoft-entra-domain-services/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-domain-services-simply-explained|Episode page}}: the full Knowledge Nugget with chapters, key quotes and FAQ
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-domain-services/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-domain-services-simply-explained|Microsoft Entra Domain Services}} – the managed Windows domain in an Azure virtual network for apps that need LDAP or Kerberos
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-domain-services-simply-explained|Microsoft Entra ID}} – the source of cloud identities, which copy one way into the managed domain
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/active-directory/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-entra-domain-services-simply-explained|Active Directory}} – the self-run domain for hybrid companies and the better choice when full domain control is needed

73986400.markup:
What happens when AI agents become the whole software team? Mirko Peters talks with Mark Smith (NZ365Guy) about his OpenClaw-based AI software factory, Ralph loops, governance and why context engineering matters more than prompts. A practical look ahead for developers, consultants and IT leaders preparing for AI-first software engineering. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Welcome and introducing Mark Smith
- 01:44 – From IT training to Dynamics CRM and Power Platform
- 08:45 – Low code superseded by AI
- 13:44 – Microsoft's AI strategy and Copilot adoption
- 21:31 – Building a nine-agent AI software factory
- 41:10 – OpenClaw, harnesses and Copilot Studio
- 44:08 – Governance, email agents and AI at the edge
- 50:19 – Preparing for an AI-first career and rapid fire

**Key takeaways**
- Mark Smith runs a nine-agent AI software factory in which each agent fills one gated role in the DevOps loop, from requirements and architecture to coding, security, release and documentation.
- Owning the agent harness with OpenClaw keeps context and data in his own {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=future-of-ai-software-factories-openclaw-mark-smith|Azure}} environment, so models from different providers can be swapped without rebuilding the system.
- For an AI-first career, Mark recommends moving from prompt engineering to context and outcomes engineering, learning about harnesses and avoiding lock-in to a single vendor.

**Worth quoting** “The day of low code has been superseded by AI. And that, I can do a lot more with a lot deeper technical functionality and technical ability.” – Mark Smith (08:45) “And so what I loved about open claw is that I own the harness, right? I can plug, as I said, I've got nine different API connections, not even including open router.” – Mark Smith (41:10) **Explore more on M365.FM**

73895529.title: Why Your Business Central Won't Scale to Finance & Operations
73895529.key: why your business central won t scale to finance operations
73895529.markup:
Many IT leaders assume a growing company can simply upgrade from Business Central to Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations later. This episode explains why that bridge does not exist, why acquisitions hit the wall hardest, and how finance and IT teams can plan a realistic phased path before a deal forces their hand. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The Business Central to F&O trap
- 02:53 – Upgrade vs. re-implementation
- 05:45 – Two systems, two design philosophies
- 13:25 – Why M&A is the real trigger
- 16:10 – Dataverse, dual-write and the patchwork
- 21:36 – Break-even: patchwork vs. migration
- 26:49 – Process redesign and data cleanup
- 41:47 – The phased path and common mistakes

**Key takeaways**
- Business Central and Finance and Operations come from different lineages (NAV and AX), so moving between them is a full re-implementation rather than an upgrade.
- Acquisitions and multi-entity consolidation are what expose the gap, and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/dataverse/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=why-your-business-central-wont-scale-to-finance-operations|Dataverse}} sync, dual-write and batch GL transfers only form a lagging patchwork.
- Plan early by designing the chart of accounts and master data for consolidation, documenting customizations and following a phased path with a parallel run.

**Worth quoting** “Business central to finance and operations isn't that. It's not a newer version of the same thing, it's a full re-implementation, and those two words carry very different weight once you understand what's actually different underneath.” – Mirko Peters (03:36) “growth in scale and growth in shape are two different things and only one of them runs you into this particular wall” – Mirko Peters (35:40) **Explore more on M365.FM**

73853268.title: PowerPoint Like a Pro- Hidden Features, Corporate Templates & Copilot with Fiona Walsh [MVP]
73853268.key: powerpoint like a pro hidden features corporate templates copilot with fiona walsh mvp
73853268.markup:
Most professionals use PowerPoint every day but miss features that have existed for years. In this interview, PowerPoint MVP Fiona Walsh shows presenters, template owners and Microsoft 365 users which fundamentals, template practices and Copilot techniques make presentations faster to build and clearer to deliver. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Intro: why PowerPoint is underestimated
- 01:00 – Fiona's path from chemistry to PowerPoint
- 04:38 – What professionals misunderstand about PowerPoint
- 08:30 – Fundamentals: alignment tools, grouping and the Selection Pane
- 18:20 – SmartArt, shortcuts and the Quick Access Toolbar
- 26:40 – Corporate templates that work
- 33:30 – Copilot in PowerPoint: strengths and limits
- 45:00 – Delivery tools, storytelling and quick-fire round

**Key takeaways**
- Many PowerPoint problems come from using one deck for different purposes: a handout read as a PDF needs a different design from slides that support a live speaker.
- Long-standing fundamentals such as the alignment tools, grouping, the Selection Pane, SmartArt conversion and the Quick Access Toolbar save time even for experienced users.
- Copilot and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/microsoft-designer/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=powerpoint-like-a-pro-hidden-features-corporate-templates-copilot-with-fiona-walsh|Designer}} work best with a robust corporate template with many layouts and image placeholders, and Copilot is especially useful for structuring ideas, finding hooks and endings, and anticipating audience questions.

**Worth quoting** “People don't tend to realize that one deck doesn't suit all different applications. And that's why PowerPoint gets the bad name.” – Fiona Walsh (03:32) “If it's a slide that I haven't created, the first thing I'd want to do is click on the selection pane because then I can see how the slide's been put together.” – Fiona Walsh (11:33) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/fiona-walsh/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=powerpoint-like-a-pro-hidden-features-corporate-templates-copilot-with-fiona-walsh|Episode page}}: the full interview with Fiona Walsh, including chapters, key quotes and FAQ

73894283.title: Microsoft Cloud PKI - Simply Explained
73894283.markup:
Shared Wi-Fi passwords and repeated VPN logins are still common in small businesses, yet running a traditional certificate infrastructure is often too much work. This episode explains certificates and Microsoft Cloud PKI in plain language and shows IT admins how Intune can deliver, renew and revoke device certificates behind the scenes. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The device access problem
- 00:46 – Why certificates exist
- 03:31 – Traditional PKI as a burden
- 06:27 – What {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/cloud-pki/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-cloud-pki-simply-explained|Microsoft Cloud PKI}} is
- 09:40 – How a device gets a certificate
- 13:09 – Where Cloud PKI fits
- 16:08 – Starting with a small pilot

**Key takeaways**
- Device certificates let managed laptops and phones prove they belong without shared Wi-Fi or VPN passwords.
- Microsoft Cloud PKI moves the root and issuing certificate authorities into {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/intune/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-cloud-pki-simply-explained|Intune}}, removing on-premises servers, NDES connectors and HSM hardware from the plan.
- Cloud PKI only covers Intune-managed devices, so start with one use case, make sure the Wi-Fi, VPN or app trusts the certificate chain, and test renewal and revocation.

**Worth quoting** “A shared Wi-Fi password can travel. Someone can write it down forward it, reuse it on a personal device, or keep it after leaving the company. A device certificate gives each managed laptop or phone its own proof instead.” – Mirko Peters (01:56) “Microsoft Cloud PKI keeps the certificate process, but shifts much of that machinery out of your server room and into the Microsoft Cloud.” – Mirko Peters (06:20) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/microsoft-cloud-pki-simply-explained/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-cloud-pki-simply-explained|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, key quotes and FAQ on Microsoft Cloud PKI
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/cloud-pki/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-cloud-pki-simply-explained|Microsoft Cloud PKI}} – the managed certificate authority service inside Intune that this episode explains end to end
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/intune/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-cloud-pki-simply-explained|Microsoft Intune}} – confirms devices are enrolled and managed, then delivers, renews and revokes their certificates
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/zero-trust/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-cloud-pki-simply-explained|Zero Trust}} – the principle that device certificates support by checking each device's proof on every request
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-cloud-pki-simply-explained|Microsoft Entra ID}} – cast as the reception desk handling sign-in identity, and a basic to check before a pilot

73892979.title: Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs) - Simply Explained
73892979.key: internal developer platforms idps simply explained
73892979.markup:
Developers often spend more time on tickets, permissions and cloud setup than on the feature they were asked to build. This episode explains internal developer platforms in plain English for IT and engineering leaders, covering golden paths, service catalogs, guardrails and how Azure tools fit behind a single self-service request. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – From tickets to self-service
- 00:46 – Why developers need a better way
- 03:37 – Golden paths
- 06:53 – The service catalog
- 09:29 – Guardrails and identity
- 13:05 – Automation behind Create Service
- 16:41 – IDP myths and where Azure fits

**Key takeaways**
- An internal developer platform is a self-service front door to approved building blocks, run by a platform team that treats developers as customers.
- Golden paths, a service catalog and guardrails built on {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=internal-developer-platforms|Entra ID}}, Azure Policy and Key Vault let teams move fast without manual approvals or unsafe shortcuts.
- An IDP is not a single portal product; start with one painful workflow and one golden path, then measure waiting time, tickets and developer feedback.

**Worth quoting** “A golden path is an approved, repeatable route for a job that teams do often. It doesn't tell every developer how to write their code.” – Mirko Peters (03:42) “If the platform says no without a route forward, people will build their own workarounds outside the platform. That creates the exact confusion the platform was meant to reduce.” – Mirko Peters (06:23) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/internal-developer-platforms/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=internal-developer-platforms|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, key quotes and FAQ on internal developer platforms
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=internal-developer-platforms|Microsoft Azure}} – supplies the compute, storage, networking, monitoring, policy and security behind the platform's golden paths
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-devops/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=internal-developer-platforms|Azure DevOps}} – one option for hosting code and running the build and release pipelines behind a service
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=internal-developer-platforms|Microsoft Entra ID}} – described as the reception desk that places developers in groups for least-privilege access

73815737.title: Why Power Platform Is Your Real Automation Layer — Not Custom Code
73815737.key: why power platform is your real automation layer not custom code
73815737.markup:
In many Dynamics 365 projects, every automation request ends up as custom code in a developer backlog, and the business pays for it every time a rule changes. This episode shows Dynamics and Power Platform teams where plug-ins still belong, how to make automation visible and owned, and how to migrate safely to Power Platform as the real automation layer. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Automation as a development backlog
- 04:25 – The hidden cost of custom code
- 08:40 – Where custom code still belongs
- 12:14 – Reasoning between event and action
- 16:46 – Sales approval without a plug-in
- 24:06 – Ownership, solutions and environments
- 35:20 – Governance, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/dlp/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=why-power-platform-is-your-real-automation-layer|DLP}} and Dataverse security
- 51:09 – Inventory, migration and a 90-day reset

**Key takeaways**
- Keep plug-ins narrow for transactional validation and performance-critical work, and move orchestration across people, systems and time into Power Platform.
- Business-critical flows need organizational identities, solutions with environment variables and managed deployments instead of personal ownership and production edits.
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/governance/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=why-power-platform-is-your-real-automation-layer|Governance}} through environments, DLP policies and Dataverse security is an operating model that lets automation scale, starting with an inventory rather than a rewrite.

**Worth quoting** “This isn't an argument against developers, it's an argument against using developers as the routing layer for every business process change.” – Mirko Peters (03:36) “Then somebody asks why dynamics feels slow to change. Dynamics isn't slow, the automation model is.” – Mirko Peters (06:24) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/why-power-platform-is-your-real-automation-layer/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=why-power-platform-is-your-real-automation-layer|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, quotes and FAQ on Dynamics automation
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/dynamics-365/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=why-power-platform-is-your-real-automation-layer|Dynamics 365}} – the application where every automation request turns into a developer backlog item and hidden custom code
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/power-platform/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=why-power-platform-is-your-real-automation-layer|Power Platform}} – proposed as the visible, owned automation layer for processes crossing people, systems and time
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/dataverse/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=why-power-platform-is-your-real-automation-layer|Dataverse}} – the event pipeline where transactional validation still belongs, plus security roles that bound automation

73819585.title: Power Platform Governance Without Killing Innovation: Security, DLP, Environments & Citizen Development with Michael Roth [MVP]
73819585.key: power platform governance without killing innovation security dlp environments citizen development with michael roth mvp
73819585.markup:
Many organizations either leave Power Platform wide open or bury makers in approvals. In this interview, Microsoft MVP Michael Roth explains to admins and platform owners how inventory, environments, DLP policies and clearly explained boundaries make governance an enabler for citizen developers rather than a brake on innovation. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Introduction to Power Platform governance
- 02:25 – Michael's path into Power Platform
- 08:30 – Platform, not just a set of tools
- 15:23 – When harmless apps become critical
- 19:31 – Governance as traffic rules
- 30:04 – Clarity, confidence and boundaries
- 40:01 – Inventory as the foundation
- 47:55 – Environments, ALM and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/dlp/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=michael-roth|DLP}}

**Key takeaways**
- Power Platform is an enterprise platform that happens to be accessible, so tenants need deliberate setup instead of open default settings.
- Governance built on clarity, confidence and explained boundaries speeds up makers and reduces shadow IT, while overly bureaucratic processes drive people away.
- Start with an inventory, structure environments, and use DLP policies, tenant settings, roles and ALM where solutions become business critical.

**Worth quoting** “So it all depends on the context, what is critical or what is not, what is secure, what is insecure, it's never the app, almost never the app, it's almost always the behavior of the people.” – Michael Roth (18:37) “If I know what will happen, if everything is clear to me, then I can choose my actions and do so. And clarity in Power Platform is exactly that.” – Michael Roth (30:50) **Explore more on M365.FM**

73814434.title: Git - Simply Explained
73814434.markup:
If your project folders are named final, final-final and use-this-one, Git is the fix. This episode explains Git in plain English for beginners, makers and Microsoft 365 builders: commits, the staging area, branches, merges, conflicts and how GitHub and pull requests fit into a team workflow. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Git is your project history
- 03:26 – The three local areas: working directory, staging area, repository
- 07:17 – Branches, merges and conflicts
- 10:46 – {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/github/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=git-simply-explained|GitHub}}, the shared online repository
- 13:55 – A Git-based team workflow
- 15:55 – CI/CD, AI and the daily route

**Key takeaways**
- Git is a local-first version control system that records deliberate, named checkpoints called commits, so you can see what changed and return to an earlier version.
- Changes move from the working directory through the staging area into the local repository, while branches let you work safely without disturbing the trusted main version.
- GitHub adds a shared remote repository and pull requests for review and automated checks, turning separate computers into one team workflow: work, stage, commit, push, review, merge.

**Worth quoting** “So think of Git as your project's memory, not a magic undo button, and not a coding language. It's a system for creating deliberate, named checkpoints that you can inspect later” – Mirko Peters (03:10) “Git is the tool that tracks your project history. GitHub is an online place where people can share that history.” – Mirko Peters (02:29) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/git-simply-explained/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=git-simply-explained|Episode page}}: the full knowledge nugget with chapters, key quotes and a short FAQ
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/github/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=git-simply-explained|GitHub}} – the shared remote repository where teams push branches and review pull requests
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-devops/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=git-simply-explained|Azure DevOps}} – named briefly as one alternative to GitHub for hosting Git repositories

73813745.title: Azure Well-Architected Framework - Simply Explained
73813745.key: azure well architected framework simply explained
73813745.markup:
Unexpected Azure bills, over-permissive apps and late-night outages often come from the decisions around a service, not the service itself. This episode explains the Azure Well-Architected Framework and its five pillars for cloud architects, developers and IT teams. You learn how to weigh trade-offs and run a practical review on one workload. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-well-architected-framework|Azure}} decisions go wrong
- 00:59 – WAF versus {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/cloud-adoption-framework/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-well-architected-framework|CAF}}
- 02:38 – Reliability
- 05:32 – Security
- 08:28 – Cost optimization
- 11:00 – Operational excellence
- 13:47 – Performance efficiency
- 16:05 – Trade-offs and the WAF review

**Key takeaways**
- The Azure Well-Architected Framework is a decision framework for one workload at a time, while the Cloud Adoption Framework prepares the shared company-wide foundation.
- Each of the five pillars forces trade-offs, so goals like cost reduction should always be phrased together with the agreed recovery and security targets.
- Start small with one important workload, run the Azure Well-Architected review and turn its recommendations into an owned, prioritized backlog.

**Worth quoting** “It isn't an Azure product you turn on. It isn't a compliance badge you earn. It's a decision framework for designing and running a workload that can hold up over time.” – Mirko Peters (00:30) “So the question isn't how much reliability can we buy. It is what level of reliability does this workload need and what are we willing to support?” – Mirko Peters (05:18) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/azure-well-architected-framework/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-well-architected-framework|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters on all five pillars, quotes and FAQ
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-well-architected-framework|Microsoft Azure}} – the platform whose workloads, bills and outages the framework helps you design around
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/cloud-adoption-framework/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-well-architected-framework|Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework}} – the company-wide foundation that prepares the airport while WAF helps one plane fly
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/zero-trust/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-well-architected-framework|Zero Trust}} – the security thinking behind checking every identity and giving the smallest access needed

73748225.title: The Copilot Assumption That's Holding You Back — Agentic RAG
73748225.key: the copilot assumption that s holding you back agentic rag
73748225.markup:
Many teams still treat Copilot as a search box and blame the tool when answers come back incomplete. This episode explains agentic RAG, the orchestration loop behind modern Copilot, for IT decision makers and Microsoft 365 architects. You learn when agentic retrieval is worth its cost, when simple retrieval wins and how to govern agents that act on their own. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The Copilot-is-search assumption
- 02:57 – Where single-shot RAG breaks
- 05:21 – What agentic RAG is and the orchestration loop
- 13:29 – Performance data and trade-offs
- 18:13 – Hybrid RAG and Copilot Wave 3
- 22:33 – Agents as digital employees
- 30:43 – {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/mcp/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=agentic-rag|MCP}} and why grounding matters
- 35:38 – Adoption, production reality and ROI

**Key takeaways**
- Agentic RAG turns the language model from a passive summarizer into a decision maker that plans, retrieves from multiple sources, evaluates results and queries again.
- Agentic RAG improves accuracy on complex multi-source tasks but costs more and runs slower, so most enterprises route simple lookups to traditional retrieval in a hybrid design.
- Autonomous agents need identity in {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/microsoft-entra/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=agentic-rag|Entra}}, oversight through Purview, audit trails and enforced grounding before they can be trusted in production.

**Worth quoting** “A system that's 10 times more expensive isn't better. It's better for something specific at a cost that has to be worth paying. The real question isn't which is better. It's which task deserves which architecture.” – Mirko Peters (15:28) “So the more freedom you give the system to reason on its own the more grounding has to be enforced not less” – Mirko Peters (34:40) **Explore more on M365.FM**
