72828653.title: Designing the Future. AI, UX, and the Next Generation of Microsoft Power Platform with Tchesco Ayih [MVP-MCT]
72828653.key: designing the future ai ux and the next generation of microsoft power platform with tchesco ayih mvp mct
72828653.markup: In {{link|https://www.m365.fm/designing-the-future-ai-ux-and-the-next-generation-of-microsoft-power-platform-with-tchesco-ayih/|https://www.m365.fm/designing-the-future-ai-ux-and-the-next-generation-of-microsoft-power-platform-with-tchesco-ayih/}} of the M365 Podcast, Mirko Peters sits down with Tchesco Ayih, Microsoft MVP, Microsoft Certified Trainer (MCT), international speaker, mentor, and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-platform-simply-explained/|https://www.m365.fm/power-platform-simply-explained/}} expert. Tchesco shares his inspiring journey into the Microsoft ecosystem, discusses the growing importance of user experience (UX) in low-code development, and explores how artificial intelligence is transforming the way organizations build business applications. From Power Apps and Dataverse to {{link|https://www.m365.fm/categories/copilot-talk/|https://www.m365.fm/categories/copilot-talk/}} Studio and AI-powered development, this conversation provides valuable insights for anyone working with Microsoft technologies, citizen development, low-code platforms, or digital transformation initiatives. Tchesco explains why beautiful design is not just a nice-to-have feature but a critical component of successful business applications, and why user-centric thinking should always come before functionality. FROM TRADITIONAL DEVELOPMENT TO MICROSOFT POWER PLATFORM Tchesco's journey into the Microsoft ecosystem started as a traditional developer with a passion for user interfaces and design. After earning Azure certifications and sharing his learning journey online, an opportunity emerged that introduced him to Microsoft Power Platform. What initially began as curiosity quickly developed into a career dedicated to helping organizations build efficient business solutions using low-code technologies. Throughout the discussion, Tchesco highlights how continuous learning, community engagement, and technical curiosity played essential roles in shaping his professional path. His story serves as a reminder that modern technology careers often evolve through experimentation, networking, and a willingness to embrace emerging platforms. THE MVP AND MCT JOURNEY Becoming a Microsoft MVP and Microsoft Certified Trainer did not happen overnight. Tchesco discusses how helping others in online communities became the foundation of his recognition within the Microsoft ecosystem. By answering technical questions, delivering community sessions, supporting Microsoft Learn Student Ambassadors, and consistently sharing knowledge, he built a reputation that eventually led to an MVP nomination. Key lessons from his journey include: - Consistently contribute to technical communities. - Share knowledge freely and help solve real problems. - Build expertise through hands-on experience. - Pursue Microsoft certifications to validate skills. - Seek mentorship from experienced professionals. - Give back to the community that helped your own growth. WHY UX IS THE SECRET INGREDIENT OF GREAT BUSINESS APPS One of the most passionate parts of the discussion centers around User Experience (UX). According to Tchesco, many Power Platform developers become overly focused on functionality and process automation while neglecting how users actually experience the application. A business process may work perfectly from a technical perspective, but if the application feels confusing, cluttered, or difficult to navigate, user adoption can suffer significantly. Tchesco argues that every application should be designed with accessibility, usability, and user satisfaction in mind. He emphasizes that developers should think beyond buttons and forms and consider: - User accessibility requirements. - Application navigation flows. - Visual hierarchy and layout. - User feedback cycles. - Readability and simplicity. - Long-term adoption and engagement. Rather than viewing UX as a separate discipline, Tchesco believes UX should be integrated into every stage of Power Platform development. DESIGN FIRST, FEATURES SECOND One of the most powerful takeaways from the conversation is Tchesco's belief that developers should begin with the user interface before implementing features. Many developers immediately start building databases, business logic, and automation workflows. However, Tchesco recommends designing the application's screens first, creating a clear structure for how users will interact with information before any technical implementation begins. A thoughtful interface helps developers: - Organize business processes logically. - Clarify data requirements. - Reduce development rework. - Improve stakeholder alignment. - Create more intuitive user journeys. - Increase overall user satisfaction. This design-first mindset helps teams build solutions that are both technically effective and enjoyable to use. UNDERSTANDING THE MICROSOFT POWER PLATFORM ECOSYSTEM For listeners new to the Power Platform, Tchesco provides a practical overview of the platform's major components and how they work together to accelerate digital transformation initiatives. The Microsoft Power Platform consists of: - Power Apps for low-code application development. - {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-automate-simply-explained/|https://www.m365.fm/power-automate-simply-explained/}} for workflow automation. - Dataverse as a scalable relational data platform. - {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-pages-simply-explained/|https://www.m365.fm/power-pages-simply-explained/}} for external-facing business websites. - Copilot Studio for conversational AI experiences. - Connectors that integrate hundreds of business systems. Together, these tools enable organizations to rapidly automate processes, modernize legacy workflows, and reduce development timelines that traditionally required months of custom coding. DATAVERSE: THE FOUNDATION OF MODERN BUSINESS SOLUTIONS The conversation explores why Dataverse has become one of the most important components of the Power Platform ecosystem. Tchesco describes Dataverse as much more than a simple database. Its relational architecture, deep integration with Microsoft services, security model, and performance capabilities make it a strong choice for enterprise-grade business applications. Compared to traditional approaches relying heavily on SharePoint lists, Dataverse enables more scalable and maintainable business solutions while supporting advanced application scenarios and automation workflows. AI, COPILOT STUDIO, AND THE FUTURE OF APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT Artificial Intelligence plays a major role throughout the discussion. Tchesco shares how AI has already transformed many aspects of his daily work, helping accelerate development, generate ideas, improve productivity, and reduce repetitive tasks. The conversation explores the growing role of: - AI-assisted development. - Prompt engineering. - Copilot Studio. - Agent-based experiences. - AI-powered business automation. - Conversational user interfaces. Rather than replacing developers, Tchesco views AI as a powerful assistant that increases productivity when used correctly. He compares AI to a junior colleague that can help complete tasks faster, while experienced professionals remain responsible for validation, governance, and final decision-making. PROMPT ENGINEERING IS BECOMING A CRITICAL SKILL One particularly interesting topic is the emergence of prompt engineering as an essential skill for modern developers. According to Tchesco, professionals who learn how to communicate effectively with AI systems will gain a significant advantage. Knowing how to provide clear context, detailed requirements, and accurate instructions can dramatically improve the quality of AI-generated outputs. As AI becomes increasingly embedded across Microsoft products and business applications, prompt-driven development is likely to become a standard part of the software development process. GOVERNANCE AND RESPONSIBLE AI ADOPTION While enthusiastic about AI's potential, Tchesco also stresses the importance of governance. Organizations must establish clear guidelines around: - Data security. - Privacy protection. - AI usage policies. - Information sharing restrictions. - Compliance requirements. - Human oversight and validation. Successful AI adoption requires balancing innovation with responsible governance. Businesses that introduce AI without adequate controls may expose sensitive information or create risks that outweigh the benefits. COMMUNITY, LEARNING, AND GIVING BACK Beyond technology, this episode highlights the importance of community engagement. Tchesco attributes much of his professional growth to the Microsoft community. By participating in forums, speaking at conferences, mentoring others, and sharing knowledge, he has developed both technical expertise and professional opportunities. His message is clear: growth accelerates when individuals actively contribute rather than simply consume information. Whether through local user groups, virtual events, online forums, or international conferences, communities remain one of the most valuable resources available to technology professionals. LOOKING AHEAD: THE FUTURE OF LOW-CODE DEVELOPMENT As the conversation concludes, Tchesco shares his perspective on the future of low-code technology. He believes low-code platforms will continue to expand rapidly over the coming years, enabling organizations to build solutions faster while empowering more people to participate in application development. At the same time, strong foundations in UX, governance, architecture, and problem-solving will remain essential. 72787365.title: Azure Bicep Fundamentals for Real Projects
72787365.key: azure bicep fundamentals for real projects
72787365.markup:
Most Bicep files are just portal clicks translated into code, which is automation, not architecture. This episode is for Azure architects and platform teams and shows how to use Bicep, deployment stacks, management groups, Azure Policy and Azure Verified Modules to build governed, predictable infrastructure that survives organizational change. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why Bicep is more than ARM with better syntax
- 03:06 – What changed in 2026
- 06:13 – The scope problem
- 09:33 – Parameters, variables and modules as contracts
- 19:02 – Deployment stacks and state management
- 23:02 – Governance at the tenant level: policy, RBAC and AVM
- 43:22 – Landing zones, environments and pipelines
- 58:32 – Bicep versus Terraform, drift and brownfield

**Key takeaways**
- Enterprise Bicep is about lifecycle, ownership and governance: scope above subscriptions, contracts enforced in parameters and modules, and state managed through deployment stacks.
- Management groups, Azure Policy and role assignments defined in {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/bicep/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-bicep-fundamentals-for-real-projects|Bicep}} let governance cascade automatically to every subscription and landing zone.
- Build on Azure Verified Modules, publish versioned modules to a registry, deploy through gated pipelines and validate continuously against drift.

**Worth quoting** “A module isn't just a reusable template. That's a technical description. A module is a contract. It says, this is how we do networking in our organization.” – Mirko Peters (12:31) “When you write bicep at management groups scope, you're not deploying resources anymore. You're defining the rules that govern how resources can be deployed.” – Mirko Peters (08:13) **Explore more on M365.FM**

- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/bicep/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-bicep-fundamentals-for-real-projects|Bicep}} – the episode's subject, presented as the vehicle for governance, deployment stacks and versioned modules
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-landing-zone/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-bicep-fundamentals-for-real-projects|Azure landing zone}} – pre-configured subscriptions composed from Bicep modules, with the ALZ reference architecture as blueprint

Generative pages promise AI-built UIs in Power Apps, but how do you get from a quick demo to something an enterprise can maintain? Microsoft MVP Sara Lagerquist explains when to extend model-driven apps with generative pages, why the code-first route beats the maker portal, and how governance and process design keep citizen-built apps under control. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Intro and Sara's journey from CRM admin to MVP
- 02:41 – Why Power Platform and model-driven apps
- 05:22 – Generative pages inside model-driven apps
- 08:04 – Maker portal vs. coding tools like VS Code
- 15:14 – Prompting, documentation and maintainability
- 21:30 – New data sources, form embedding and PCF
- 26:52 – Governance, citizen development and the CoE
- 34:56 – Community Sweden, speaking and career advice

**Key takeaways**
- Generative pages let you keep the out-of-the-box strengths of a model-driven app and extend only the UI where it falls short.
- For production-ready generative pages, build them through a coding tool such as VS Code with {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/github-copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=beyond-prompt-a-page-building-enterprise-ready-ai-experiences-in-power-apps-with-sara-lagerquist|GitHub Copilot}} and Microsoft's skill rather than the maker portal, which is best for trying things out.
- As AI makes app creation fast, the hard parts become process design, adoption and governance, so makers should invest in designing processes first.

**Worth quoting** “So the combination of all the benefits of model driven apps plus a gen page is like the future of apps.” – Sara Lagerquist (07:25) “I would say the UI way of doing it, the maker portal way of doing it, it's mostly for trying it out and maybe at most doing a proof of concept maybe.” – Sara Lagerquist (10:06) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72786704.title: ARM Templates Were a Mistake: Lessons from the Bicep Shift
72786704.key: arm templates were a mistake lessons from the bicep shift
72786704.markup:
Portal clicks feel fast, but they quietly create configuration drift that breaks governance at scale. This episode is for Azure architects and platform teams deciding between ARM, Bicep and Terraform, and it explains how infrastructure as code, policy as code and guardrails keep both humans and AI agents under control. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The death of ClickOps and configuration drift
- 07:22 – From imperative to declarative infrastructure
- 10:26 – ARM templates: the necessary mistake and cognitive load
- 17:48 – Bicep: designed for humans, compiled for machines
- 23:56 – Drift as a governance epidemic and IaC as the control plane
- 30:41 – AI agents, guardrails and Bicep vs. Terraform
- 41:44 – Governance as an operating model and continuous compliance
- 55:14 – Infrastructure as intent, lessons and next steps for leaders

**Key takeaways**
- Configuration drift from manual portal changes is a governance failure, and only declarative infrastructure as code makes the actual state visible, reviewable and correctable.
- Bicep compiles to ARM JSON but removes its syntax noise, which is why new {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=arm-templates-were-a-mistake-lessons-from-the-bicep-shift|Azure}} projects default to it while legacy ARM templates persist because of switching costs.
- AI agents can generate infrastructure code quickly, but it must flow through policy as code, human review and CI/CD so that automation never outpaces control.

**Worth quoting** “If you treat it like a technical problem, you'll miss what's actually happening. You'll spend money on tools and miss the structural failure underneath because drift is a governance failure.” – Mirko Peters (04:00) “AI agents must operate within policy guardrails, not autonomously, not with broad permissions, not trusted to make security decisions without oversight. They generate proposals, policies validate those proposals, humans review the validated output.” – Mirko Peters (34:06) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/arm-templates-were-a-mistake-lessons-from-the-bicep-shift/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=arm-templates-were-a-mistake-lessons-from-the-bicep-shift|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, key quotes and an FAQ on Bicep and drift
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/bicep/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=arm-templates-were-a-mistake-lessons-from-the-bicep-shift|Bicep}} – the Azure-native language that compiles to ARM JSON while removing its syntax noise
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/infrastructure-as-code/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=arm-templates-were-a-mistake-lessons-from-the-bicep-shift|Infrastructure as code}} – presented as the governance control plane that makes drift visible and correctable
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/governance/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=arm-templates-were-a-mistake-lessons-from-the-bicep-shift|Governance}} – reframed from approval gates to an operating model of structural controls, policy and enforcement

72828100.title: Can Google Sheets Beat Excel: Microsoft MVP David Benaim Settles the Debate
72828100.key: can google sheets beat excel microsoft mvp david benaim settles the debate
72828100.markup:
Excel has been around for 40 years, yet Google Sheets now matches or beats it in several areas that many Microsoft-centric teams overlook. In this conversation Excel MVP and comedian David Benaim compares tables, formulas, collaboration, scripting and AI assistants in both tools to help analysts and business users choose the right spreadsheet for each job. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Meet David Benaim, the Excel comedian
- 06:47 – Is Excel dead? A short history of spreadsheets
- 12:34 – Google Sheets vs. Excel: tables, Power Query and collaboration
- 21:30 – AI in spreadsheets: Copilot, Claude and Gemini
- 28:11 – Formulas, VBA, Office Scripts and Apps Script
- 33:08 – From Power Pivot to Power BI
- 42:35 – Spreadsheet bugs, comedy and the future of spreadsheets
- 50:49 – Rapid-fire round

**Key takeaways**
- Neither tool simply wins: Excel leads with {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/power-query/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=can-google-sheets-beat-excel-with-david-benaim|Power Query}}, Power Pivot and the Microsoft ecosystem, while Google Sheets has more functions, group-by views and friction-free collaboration across organizations.
- AI is reshaping spreadsheets fast, from Copilot's editing agent and Claude's Excel add-in to Gemini features in Google Sheets such as smart fill and canvas views.
- Spreadsheets will still exist in ten years, and the most valuable habit to adopt now is using proper tables in either Excel or Google Sheets.

**Worth quoting** “spreadsheets in general allow for that flexibility that I think the office employee is going to want for the very, very foreseeable future.” – David Benaim (07:53) “I think that Excel has power query and power query is absolutely game-changing. And for that reason, until Google sheets has an equivalent, I will favor Excel.” – David Benaim (14:54) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/can-google-sheets-beat-excel-microsoft-mvp-david-benaim-settles-the-debate/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=can-google-sheets-beat-excel-with-david-benaim|Episode page}}: the full conversation with chapters, quotes and FAQ on Excel versus Google Sheets

This episode shows sales leaders and Dynamics 365 architects how to connect LinkedIn and Dynamics 365 with Sales Navigator, relationship health scoring, Copilot and orchestrated agents while staying within rate limits, GDPR and good governance. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why your CRM is blind
- 02:40 – The three disconnects
- 06:07 – LinkedIn APIs, Sales Navigator sync and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/power-automate/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=linkedin-dynamics-365-the-architecture-of-modern-selling|Power Automate}}
- 16:49 – Native integration and relationship health
- 22:54 – Copilot for Sales and sales agents
- 29:20 – Orchestration, rate limits and timeouts
- 41:49 – Governance, roadmap and the changing seller role
- 64:28 – Multi-agent B2B and the risks

**Key takeaways**
- LinkedIn holds the relationship graph and Dynamics 365 holds the process, so modern selling needs an architecture that connects them through official channels such as Sales Navigator CRM sync.
- Relationship health scoring, Copilot for Sales and orchestrated sales agents turn synced data into insight and action, but they must be designed around API rate limits, timeouts and governance.
- Roll out in phases, treat LinkedIn data like regulated data and keep humans reviewing agent decisions to manage hallucination, bias and over-reliance risks.

**Worth quoting** “Your CRM is a database of records, but your actual business is a network of relationships.” – Mirko Peters (01:47) “GDPR does not care how clever your integration is. 72771493.title: Azure Networking Unlocked: Secure Azure Functions, Virtual Network Manager & Infrastructure as Code with Rex de Koning [MVP-MCT]
72771493.key: azure networking unlocked secure azure functions virtual network manager infrastructure as code with rex de koning mvp mct
72771493.markup:
Many teams assume Microsoft takes care of networking in the cloud, then find gaps in security and routing later. Azure MVP Rex de Koning explains to cloud architects and admins how Azure networking really works, from hub-and-spoke and Virtual Network Manager to securing Azure Functions. You come away with practical guidance on building network foundations with infrastructure as code. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why networking is the foundation
- 02:11 – Rex's path into Azure
- 06:54 – Azure networking misconceptions and topologies
- 13:50 – Azure Virtual Network Manager
- 24:22 – Landing zones and infrastructure as code
- 42:01 – Securing Azure Functions
- 51:19 – Final advice

**Key takeaways**
- In Azure, routing happens at the resource level, so network security groups remain essential even behind a central firewall.
- Azure Virtual Network Manager centralizes IP address management, connectivity, security admin rules and routing across many virtual networks.
- Deploy networks and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-functions/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=azure-networking-unlocked-secure-azure-functions-virtual-network-manager-infrastructure-as-code|Azure Functions}} through infrastructure as code with private endpoints and VNet integration, and feed any emergency portal fix back into code.

**Worth quoting** “And with Azure Virtual Network Manager, you have basically an admin rule that you can push towards all network security groups that are connected to the Azure Virtual Network Manager.” – Rex de Koning (17:34) “So if you set it up in infrastructure as code that it has multiple advantages, it will always set things up always in the same way that you want it.” – Rex de Koning (30:03) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72737981.title: The PowerShell Ceiling: Why You Need Bicep
72737981.key: the powershell ceiling why you need bicep
72737981.markup:
You have dozens of PowerShell scripts that work, but nobody could rebuild the platform behind them in three hours. This episode is for Microsoft 365 and Azure automation engineers who have hit the scripting ceiling. Learn how Bicep turns infrastructure and identity into versioned, auditable code and how to start the transition next Monday. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – 50 Scripts Nobody Can Govern

72767166.title: Everything Microsoft Didn't Tell You About Teams with Everything Microsoft Didn't Tell You About Teams with Josh Blalock [MVP]
72767166.key: everything microsoft didn t tell you about teams with everything microsoft didn t tell you about teams with josh blalock mvp
72767166.markup:
Most organizations still treat meeting-room audio as an afterthought, even though Copilot now depends on it. In this episode, Microsoft MVP Josh Blalock explains to IT leaders and meeting-room planners how Teams evolved from Skype for Business, why audio beats video, what Teams certification really means and how to plan rooms that give AI clean data. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Welcome and Josh's path from Air Force IT to unified communications
- 03:39 – From Skype for Business to Microsoft Teams
- 06:12 – Becoming an MVP and the Shure Ignition program
- 17:55 – Why audio matters more than video
- 23:36 – Hardware vs. software: onboard DSPs and cloud audio processing
- 30:42 – Teams certified devices and why certification matters
- 34:48 – Planning meeting rooms for challenging acoustics
- 40:10 – Comms vNext and Josh's next chapter

**Key takeaways**
- In AI-enabled meetings, audio is no longer just sound but the real-time data {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=everything-microsoft-didnt-tell-you-about-teams-with-josh-blalock-mvp|Copilot}} uses for summaries, action items and documents, so 'good enough' audio limits your AI investment.
- Clean audio should be produced in the room, for example by onboard software DSPs in microphones and room kits, before Microsoft Teams processes it in the cloud.
- Teams certified devices pass rigorous Microsoft testing and are the supported option, and complex rooms still benefit from an integrator, a proof of concept and acoustic treatment.

**Worth quoting** “If your video fails, it's okay. The meeting can still go on. You can still hear people with audio. If your audio fails, now you're done. Your meeting is over.” – Josh Blalock (19:48) “It's no longer just spoken words and audio. 72671880.title: Beyond the Portal: The Strategic Architecture of Microsoft Graph and PowerShell
72671880.key: beyond the portal the strategic architecture of microsoft graph and powershell
72671880.markup:
Clicking through admin portals does not scale to thousands of users, devices and sites, and legacy APIs are being retired. This episode is for Microsoft 365 administrators and architects who want to move from portal operations to Graph- and PowerShell-driven automation. You learn how Graph works underneath the portals, how to automate safely and why permission hygiene decides whether Copilot and agents succeed. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why portals fail at enterprise scale
- 03:04 – What Microsoft Graph actually is
- 06:08 – Authentication, permissions and least privilege
- 09:13 – User lifecycle and the collaboration layer at scale
- 16:35 – Security, governance, compliance and reporting via Graph
- 26:24 – Delta queries, permission debt, policy as code and idempotency
- 38:41 – Case studies, Copilot, agents and the skills gap
- 50:22 – Deadlines, roadmap, authentication patterns, operations and first steps

**Key takeaways**
- Every Microsoft 365 portal is a wrapper around Microsoft Graph, so Graph and PowerShell are the real control plane for automation, governance, security and reporting at scale.
- Safe Graph automation depends on least-privilege application permissions, certificates or managed identities instead of client secrets, idempotent scripts, delta queries or {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/change-notifications/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=beyond-the-portal-the-strategic-architecture-of-microsoft-graph-and-powershell|webhooks}} instead of polling, and respect for throttling.
- Copilot and AI agents inherit existing permissions, so permission hygiene, policy as code and monitoring through Graph activity and audit logs are prerequisites, while retirements such as Azure AD Graph and the Graph CLI force migration.

**Worth quoting** “The portal is just a convenience layer. Graph is your control plane. PowerShell is the engine that makes it work at enterprise scale.” – Mirko Peters (69:10) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/beyond-the-portal-the-strategic-architecture-of-microsoft-graph-and-powershell/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=beyond-the-portal-the-strategic-architecture-of-microsoft-graph-and-powershell|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, quotes, deadlines and a practical starting roadmap
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/graph/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=beyond-the-portal-the-strategic-architecture-of-microsoft-graph-and-powershell|Microsoft Graph}} – the control plane behind every Microsoft 365 portal and the core of every automation pattern discussed
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=beyond-the-portal-the-strategic-architecture-of-microsoft-graph-and-powershell|Microsoft 365 Copilot}} – why permission debt surfaces through Copilot and why permission hygiene must come before rollout

72786209.title: Think Like an Attacker: Microsoft Security Exposure Management with Uros Babic [MVP-MCT]
72786209.key: think like an attacker microsoft security exposure management with uros babic mvp mct
72786209.markup:
Many security teams still fix vulnerabilities in isolation while attackers chain them into paths to domain or global admin. Mirko plays the attacker against Microsoft Security MVP Uros Babic, who shows security teams and decision makers how exposure management, attack paths and Security Copilot change the defense. You learn how to prioritize real risk and measure exposure instead of activity. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Thinking like an attacker
- 08:55 – Uros's path into cybersecurity
- 16:39 – {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/ai-agent/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=think-like-an-attacker-microsoft-security-exposure-management-with-uros-babic-mvp-mct|AI agents}} and elevation of privilege
- 23:13 – Zero trust in the age of AI
- 27:40 – Exposure management and Security Copilot
- 42:14 – MITRE ATT&CK and attack behavior
- 46:08 – Security posture and the right KPIs
- 52:00 – Phishing, lateral movement and rapid fire

**Key takeaways**
- Attackers chain misconfigurations, vulnerabilities and excessive permissions into attack paths, so teams should fix what is actually exploitable first rather than everything at once.
- Zero trust reduces trust, while Microsoft Security Exposure Management shows where an organization is still exposed, especially around tier-zero assets and AI agents.
- Modern SOC metrics should measure exposure reduction, such as time to remediate critical exposure, instead of ticket and alert volume.

**Worth quoting** “it is very important to going to think like what you mentioned, like attacker, and understand not just what is vulnerable, but what is actually exposed, publicly exposed.” – Uros Babic (02:46) “the key idea it is not about the fixing everything it is about fixing what attacker really exploit the first” – Uros Babic (12:56) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/think-like-an-attacker-microsoft-security-exposure-management-with-uros-babic-mvp-mct/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=think-like-an-attacker-microsoft-security-exposure-management-with-uros-babic-mvp-mct|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, quotes and FAQ on exposure management
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/uros-babic/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=think-like-an-attacker-microsoft-security-exposure-management-with-uros-babic-mvp-mct|Uros Babic}} – Microsoft Security MVP and MCT who defends against Mirko's attacker role using exposure management

72561753.title: Stop Building Bots, Start Building Runtimes: A Field Guide to Microsoft Agents
72561753.key: stop building bots start building runtimes a field guide to microsoft agents
72561753.markup:
Many organizations are building fragile agents without governance, duplicating work and losing track of what runs in their tenant. This field guide is for IT leaders, architects and makers who need to make sense of Microsoft's agent landscape after Build 2026. You get a four-layer model plus practical guidance on Agent 365, Entra Agent ID, Foundry Agent Service and grounding. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – From chatbots to agents that operate
- 00:51 – The four layers of agents
- 03:26 – Build 2026: agents become infrastructure
- 06:51 – The experience layer
- 09:57 – The agent layer
- 13:47 – Runtime, governance and orchestration
- 28:14 – Shadow agents, identity and integration
- 59:03 – Getting started, failures and roadmap

**Key takeaways**
- Think of Microsoft agents as four layers, experience, agent, runtime and governance, each with different owners and controls, instead of picking products at random.
- Agent 365 and Entra Agent ID turn agents into governed identities with least-privilege access, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/conditional-access/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=stop-building-bots-start-building-runtimes-a-field-guide-to-microsoft-agents|conditional access}}, audit trails and instant revocation, which addresses shadow agents.
- Start with one well-scoped agent in Copilot Studio grounded in your own data, register it in Agent 365, measure its impact and graduate it to Foundry for scale.

**Worth quoting** “Stop thinking about agents as products. Start thinking about them as a system with four layers. Each layer has different needs.” – Mirko Peters (01:12) “You are not just using an agent anymore. You are hiring one. It comes with all the governance machinery that you would expect when hiring any other system.” – Mirko Peters (04:41) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72754345.title: EXTENSIBILITY FIRST: Building .NET Systems That Survive Change with Miguel Castro [MVP]
72754345.key: extensibility first building net systems that survive change with miguel castro mvp
72754345.markup:
Why do some enterprise applications become impossible to change while others keep evolving for years? .NET architect Miguel Castro explains how extensibility, plug-in hooks and the strategy pattern keep systems maintainable, drawing on lessons from ASP.NET and a real live-transcription platform. A practical conversation for developers and architects who want software that survives change. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Introducing {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/miguel-castro/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=extensibility-first-building-net-systems-that-survive-change-with-miguel-castro-mvp|Miguel Castro}}
- 01:24 – From VB to .NET
- 05:06 – What makes great architecture
- 21:56 – Why extensibility: lessons from ASP.NET
- 35:14 – Design patterns and abstraction
- 41:21 – Real-world example: live transcription plug-ins
- 48:42 – How projects and automation begin
- 56:21 – Rapid fire and AI coding

**Key takeaways**
- Enterprise systems become hard to maintain mainly because they were not designed to allow enhancement and modification, which is exactly what extensibility addresses.
- Extensible designs rest on abstraction: strategy-style interfaces, plug-in hooks and dependency injection let parts be swapped without touching the core pipeline.
- AI can speed up writing small components, but architecture and design based on client requirements still need a human architect.

**Worth quoting** “One right on top of the other. I don't think you can write clean code without designing a good system first.” – Miguel Castro (06:55) “If I had to nail one thing, it's probably that they're not designed in a way that allows enhancement and modification later in an easy way. And that's where the topic of extensibility comes in.” – Miguel Castro (10:07) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72561540.title: The Death of the UI: Why CUA is the End of SaaS as We Know It
72561540.key: the death of the ui why cua is the end of saas as we know it
72561540.markup:
If agents can do the work that once required people clicking through screens, the user interface and the per-seat SaaS model lose their foundation. This episode is for IT leaders, enterprise architects and software decision makers planning for agent-driven operations. You learn what agents actually need, where computer-using agents fit, and how to govern, measure and scale them. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The UI was always a workaround and seat-based pricing breaks
- 06:44 – What agents actually require and the API-first imperative
- 13:28 – Workflow capital as the real moat
- 17:23 – Non-human identities and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/agent-365/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-ui-why-cua-is-the-end-of-saas-as-we-know-it|Agent 365}} as the control plane
- 23:00 – Foundry Agent Service and computer-using agents as the bridge
- 29:44 – Safety, observability, skills, ROI and ownership
- 43:45 – Operations, incident response and continuous improvement
- 52:44 – Investment case, strategic choices, roadmap and culture

**Key takeaways**
- Agents do not need dashboards; they need stable APIs, explicit business logic, context and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/governance/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-ui-why-cua-is-the-end-of-saas-as-we-know-it|governance}}, which puts seat-based SaaS pricing and UI-first architectures under pressure.
- Computer-using agents can bridge legacy systems without APIs, but their success rate drops sharply on complex multi-step workflows, so API-first modernization remains the long-term goal.
- Running agents at scale needs agent identities with zero standing privilege, a control plane such as Agent 365, a runtime such as Foundry Agent Service, clear ownership, kill switches and continuous evaluation.

**Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/the-death-of-the-ui-why-cua-is-the-end-of-saas-as-we-know-it/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-ui-why-cua-is-the-end-of-saas-as-we-know-it|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, takeaways and an FAQ on agents replacing UI-first software

- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/foundry-agent-service/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-ui-why-cua-is-the-end-of-saas-as-we-know-it|Foundry Agent Service}} – the runtime for orchestrated multi-agent workflows, with built-in tracing and computer use as a tool

72740005.key: microsoft copilot adoption what actually works with chris hinch microsoft
72740005.markup:
Many organizations buy Microsoft 365 Copilot and expect users to figure it out on their own. In this interview, Microsoft cloud solutions architect Chris Hinch explains for IT leaders and adoption owners what separates successful rollouts from failed ones, from pain-point use cases and champions programs to prompting, governance and security. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Chris Hinch's path to Microsoft
- 05:52 – Copilot is not a magic bullet
- 10:04 – What makes adoption succeed
- 16:06 – Pilot groups and champions
- 22:03 – Copilot, Copilot Studio and Foundry
- 25:09 – Measuring success and prompting
- 31:59 – Security, governance and readiness
- 45:23 – Where Copilot is heading

**Key takeaways**
- Copilot adoption succeeds when it starts from department pain points and comes with real training, not when AI is rolled out for its own sake.
- A champions program spreads working prompts across departments and creates internal advocates for the wider rollout.
- Copilot respects user permissions, so poor governance becomes visible; tools like SharePoint Advanced Management, Purview, Entra and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/defender/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-copilot-adoption-what-actually-works-with-chris-hinch-microsoft|Defender}} help close those gaps.

**Worth quoting** “You need proper training on how to ask the questions in a way to get to the outcome that you're wanting quicker.” – Chris Hinch (13:05) “No, the agent's fine. It's the knowledge that you're pointing to it. So it's more you need to understand the holistic thing of everything that you're wanting the agent to do.” – Chris Hinch (23:57) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72561184.key: the agentic operating model beyond the copilot hype
72561184.markup:
Many organizations think they are transforming with AI but are really just deploying chat interfaces over search. This episode shows architects and IT leaders how Work IQ, Agent 365, Entra Agent ID and the A2A protocol form an agentic operating model, and what it really costs in governance, identity and Copilot Credits. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why RAG hits the latency wall
- 03:44 – Static vs. liquid context and Work IQ
- 07:15 – The service account trap and stalled {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-agentic-operating-model-beyond-the-copilot-hype|Copilot}} pilots
- 13:25 – Entra Agent ID and policy as code

72738820.title: Planner Beyond Tasks: Building Enterprise Project & Portfolio Management with Erik van Hurck [MVP]
72738820.key: planner beyond tasks building enterprise project portfolio management with erik van hurck mvp
72738820.markup:
Project management has evolved far beyond spreadsheets, email chains, and standalone task lists. As organizations grow, managing hundreds of concurrent projects, allocating resources effectively, tracking financial performance, and aligning initiatives with business strategy become increasingly difficult. While Microsoft Planner has become a popular solution for everyday task management, many organizations wonder whether it can also support enterprise-scale Project and Portfolio Management (PPM). In {{link|https://www.m365.fm/planner-beyond-tasks-building-enterprise-project-portfolio-management-with-erik-van-hurck-mvp/|this episode}}, Microsoft MVP Erik van Hurck shares his extensive experience helping medium and large enterprises transform Microsoft Planner into a powerful project management ecosystem using the {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-platform-simply-explained/|Power Platform}}, Dataverse, and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/categories/power-platform-talk/|Microsoft 365}}. Together, we explore the future of project management, portfolio governance, AI-powered PMOs, and why successful project delivery requires much more than simply assigning tasks. **THE EVOLUTION OF PROJECT MANAGEMENT IN MICROSOFT 365 ** Project management within the Microsoft ecosystem has changed dramatically over the past two decades. Organizations once relied almost exclusively on Microsoft Project and Excel before newer collaboration tools like Microsoft Teams, Planner, Power BI, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-apps-simply-explained/|Power Apps}}, and Azure DevOps introduced more flexible ways of managing work. Today, companies often operate with multiple project management solutions simultaneously. Marketing teams may prefer Planner, software developers work in Azure DevOps, business units adopt Jira or Trello, while executives require portfolio-level reporting across every initiative. This growing diversity creates significant visibility challenges that traditional project management tools alone cannot solve. **UNDERSTANDING WHERE MICROSOFT PLANNER FITS ** Microsoft Planner was originally designed as a lightweight task management solution that integrates seamlessly with Microsoft Teams. Its intuitive Kanban boards, collaborative task lists, and easy user experience made it one of the fastest-growing Microsoft 365 applications during the remote work boom. However, enterprise project management requires considerably more functionality than task tracking alone. Organizations need financial management, resource allocation, risk registers, lessons learned, governance processes, executive reporting, portfolio visibility, and strategic planning capabilities. Planner excels at managing work execution, but enterprise PMOs require an additional management layer capable of coordinating projects across the entire organization. **BUILDING ENTERPRISE PROJECT PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT WITH THE POWER PLATFORM** Rather than replacing Microsoft Planner, Erik explains how organizations can extend it using Microsoft Dataverse, Model-Driven Power Apps, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-automate-simply-explained/|Power Automate}}, and Power BI. This creates a flexible enterprise Project & Portfolio Management solution that integrates naturally with Microsoft 365 while remaining highly customizable for each organization's unique requirements. Instead of forcing companies into rigid software processes, the Power Platform allows consultants to model governance, financial management, reporting structures, resource planning, and business workflows directly around existing organizational practices. Key platform capabilities include:
- Enterprise portfolio management
- Financial tracking
- Resource management
- Risk management
- Executive dashboards

**WHY PROJECTS, PROGRAMS, AND PORTFOLIOS ARE DIFFERENT ** One of the most valuable insights from this discussion is understanding the distinction between projects, programs, and portfolios. While many organizations treat these concepts interchangeably, each represents a different management layer with unique responsibilities. Individual projects deliver specific outcomes within defined budgets and timelines. Programs coordinate multiple related projects toward a common objective, while portfolios oversee strategic investment across entire departments, business units, or organizational initiatives. This layered approach provides executives with visibility far beyond individual project status reports, enabling better strategic decision-making, investment prioritization, and organizational governance. **CONNECTING PLANNER WITH THE ENTIRE MICROSOFT ECOSYSTEM ** Modern enterprises rarely rely on a single project management application. Instead, Planner frequently coexists alongside Azure DevOps, Microsoft Project, SAP, Jira, SharePoint, Teams, Power BI, and other business systems. Rather than replacing these platforms, enterprise portfolio management solutions integrate data from multiple sources into a unified reporting and governance layer. Through Microsoft Graph APIs, Dataverse, and Power Platform connectors, organizations gain a comprehensive view of projects regardless of where day-to-day work is actually managed. **AI IS TRANSFORMING PROJECT MANAGEMENT ** Artificial Intelligence is rapidly changing how project managers operate. Rather than replacing experienced professionals, AI acts as an intelligent assistant that dramatically reduces administrative work while improving decision quality. Large Language Models can generate project documentation, summarize meetings, create status reports, recommend project risks, analyze lessons learned, and surface historical knowledge from previous initiatives. This allows project managers to spend less time producing documentation and more time leading teams, removing blockers, and delivering successful outcomes. AI is particularly valuable for:
- Automatic status reporting
- Risk identification
- Lessons learned analysis
- Document generation
- Project planning assistance

**GOVERNANCE REMAINS THE FOUNDATION ** As AI gains greater access to enterprise data, governance becomes increasingly important. Organizations must carefully control permissions, define security boundaries, and ensure AI systems only access information appropriate for each user. Enterprise project management extends beyond delivering projects on time—it also requires protecting sensitive financial information, confidential business initiatives, resource allocation, and executive reporting. Proper governance within Microsoft 365, Microsoft Graph, Dataverse, and the Power Platform ensures organizations can safely leverage AI without compromising security or compliance. **THE FUTURE OF THE PROJECT MANAGEMENT OFFICE (PMO) ** The traditional PMO is evolving from an administrative function into a strategic business partner powered by automation and AI. Future project managers will rely heavily on digital assistants capable of drafting documentation, identifying risks, recommending improvements, and continuously learning from previous projects. Rather than replacing human expertise, AI enables project managers to focus on leadership, stakeholder communication, strategic planning, and team success. Organizations that successfully combine Microsoft Planner, Power Platform, Dataverse, AI, and strong governance will create PMOs capable of delivering greater visibility, improved decision-making, and significantly higher project success rates. **FINAL THOUGHTS ** Microsoft Planner has grown far beyond its origins as a lightweight task management application. When combined with the Power Platform, Dataverse, Microsoft Graph, Power BI, and AI, it becomes the foundation for sophisticated enterprise Project & Portfolio Management solutions capable of supporting even the most complex organizations. As Erik van Hurck explains throughout this conversation, successful project management is no longer about simply tracking tasks—it's about connecting strategy, governance, resources, financial planning, and intelligent automation into one integrated platform that helps organizations deliver projects faster, smarter, and with greater confidence Become a supporter of this podcast: {{link|https://www.spreaker.com/podcast/m365-fm-microsoft-365-azure-cloud-power-platform-ai--6704921/support?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss|https://www.spreaker.com/podcast/m365-fm-microsoft-365-azure-cloud-power-platform-ai--6704921/support}}.

72560889.title: Beyond Binary Governance: Managing the Copilot-to-Quantum Pipeline
72560889.key: beyond binary governance managing the copilot to quantum pipeline
72560889.markup:
Your AI governance is built on binary rules, Copilot reasons in probabilities, and quantum computing will add a third logic entirely. This episode shows M365 governance and Azure architecture leaders why quantum-safe cryptography, crypto agility and hybrid governance gates have to be designed now, before quantum-classical workloads go live. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The wrong assumption behind enterprise AI
- 03:57 – Why probabilistic AI is a liability
- 07:38 – The Copilot trap
- 10:54 – The quantum-safe cliff
- 13:48 – Agent fabric and the three layers of hybrid governance
- 22:34 – Crypto agility, identity and key management
- 30:06 – Gates, audit trails and regulation
- 68:20 – Immediate action items and the governance paradox

**Key takeaways**
- Classical M365 governance is binary, Copilot and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/ai-agent/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=beyond-binary-governance-managing-the-copilot-to-quantum-pipeline|AI agents}} are probabilistic, and quantum adds superposition, so governance must be redesigned to span all three.
- Harvest-now-decrypt-later makes long-lived M365 data vulnerable today, so organizations need a cryptography inventory, confidentiality horizons and a crypto agility roadmap.
- Hybrid quantum-classical workloads need decision gates, quantum-safe identity and key management, end-to-end audit trails and portability before any pilot touches real data.

**Worth quoting** “The architecture required to prepare for quantum computing is fundamentally incompatible with how you're building AI systems today. This is not a technical problem. It's a governance problem.” – Mirko Peters (00:28) “Co-pilot isn't the endpoint. It's the entry point to a much larger orchestration problem that most organizations haven't mapped yet.” – Mirko Peters (07:54) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72667984.title: The IaC Trap:Terraform vs. Bicep – Which One Wins?
72667984.key: the iac trap terraform vs bicep which one wins
72667984.markup:
Choosing between Terraform and Bicep is rarely just a syntax decision: each tool embeds an operational model with real costs for security, governance and team structure. This episode is for Azure architects, platform engineers and IT leaders deciding on infrastructure as code. Learn how state files, drift, Azure Policy, OpenTofu licensing and hybrid patterns should shape your decision. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/terraform/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-iac-trap-terraform-vs-bicep-which-one-wins|Terraform}} state file as an unplanned database
- 06:12 – The multi-cloud myth and the day-zero gap
- 12:24 – {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/bicep/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-iac-trap-terraform-vs-bicep-which-one-wins|Bicep}}'s stateless model and what-if
- 19:12 – Modules, AVM and state as governance
- 26:01 – Drift detection and Azure Policy integration
- 33:28 – Operational cost and the skill set divergence
- 40:17 – OpenTofu, licensing and multi-team coordination
- 52:03 – AI guardrails, platform engineering and the decision framework

**Key takeaways**
- Terraform's state file is a database you have to secure, lock, back up and reconcile, while Bicep delegates state to Azure Resource Manager.
- Bicep gets new Azure features on day zero and hits Azure Policy before resources exist, whereas Terraform trades that depth for multi-cloud reach.
- The right {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/infrastructure-as-code/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-iac-trap-terraform-vs-bicep-which-one-wins|IaC}} choice depends on your real cloud strategy, team structure and licensing stance, and governance quality matters more than the tool itself.

72560443.title: Architecture Over Chat: Building the Agent Fabric
72560443.key: architecture over chat building the agent fabric
72560443.markup:
Most organizations think they have AI agents, but what they really have are chatbots that forget everything when the window closes. This episode is for architects and IT leaders planning enterprise agents on the Microsoft stack. It lays out the agent fabric blueprint, from GitHub Copilot SDK session persistence to Entra Agent IDs, orchestration, cost routing and Agent 365 governance. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Chatbots trapped in tabs
- 02:52 – The silo problem and why chat is wrong
- 09:03 – Session persistence and multi-device
- 14:41 – The GitHub Copilot SDK blueprint
- 18:00 – Identity, orchestration and memory governance
- 28:10 – Cost curve and model routing
- 34:50 – Agent 365, interoperability and security
- 67:14 – Implementation path and risks

**Key takeaways**
- Enterprise agents fail not because models are weak but because they are built as stateless, siloed chat interfaces instead of persistent system participants.
- A working agent fabric needs session persistence, a shared backend with thin clients, a dedicated {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/agent-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=architecture-over-chat-building-the-agent-fabric|Entra Agent ID}} per agent, explicit orchestration and model routing to control cost.
- Persistent memory and agent-to-agent calls create new risks such as memory poisoning and data leakage, which require Agent 365 governance, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/dlp/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=architecture-over-chat-building-the-agent-fabric|DLP}} by design, sandboxing and causal observability.

**Worth quoting** “Chat is stateless by design. Every turn is independent. You ask, it responds done. But agents don't work that way. Agents require state. They need memory across sessions.” – Mirko Peters (01:47) “An agent without an identity is a ghost. You can't audit it. You can't control it. You can't govern it.” – Mirko Peters (18:00) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/architecture-over-chat-building-the-agent-fabric/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=architecture-over-chat-building-the-agent-fabric|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, quotes and a FAQ on the agent fabric
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/ai-agent/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=architecture-over-chat-building-the-agent-fabric|AI agent}} – the episode argues most agents are stateless chatbots and need persistence, identity and orchestration

- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/github-copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=architecture-over-chat-building-the-agent-fabric|GitHub Copilot}} – its SDK serves as the blueprint: one agent runtime, thin clients and built-in session persistence

72666258.key: the end of data entry why your business logic is moving to agents

Sales reps, controllers and buyers still spend hours copying data between email, CRM and ERP. This episode is for business and IT leaders working with Dynamics 365 and the Power Platform, and it explains how Dataverse-grounded agents take over data entry, reconciliation and routing while staying inside your security and governance rules. **In this episode**

72560250.title: Stop Treating Agents Like Service Accounts
72560250.key: stop treating agents like service accounts
72560250.markup:
Your organization is deploying AI agents under service accounts built for static apps, creating invisible, over-privileged identities. This episode is for identity, security and governance teams who need to bring agents under control, using Entra Agent ID, blueprints, conditional access and an agent registry without slowing teams down. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why service accounts were never built for agents
- 03:24 – The shadow AI explosion and the identity vacuum
- 08:48 – The cost of the old model and why RBAC fails
- 16:26 – Three identity types and the blueprint hierarchy
- 21:07 – {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/conditional-access/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=stop-treating-agents-like-service-accounts|Conditional access}}, agent registry and the agent fabric
- 30:31 – Least privilege, observability and blueprints in practice
- 41:04 – Lifecycle, discovery, incident response and unified AI policy
- 52:48 – Speed vs. security, roles, ROI and the roadmap

**Key takeaways**
- AI agents are a third identity type between users and workloads, and forcing them into service principals creates over-privileged God accounts with invisible blast radius.
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/agent-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=stop-treating-agents-like-service-accounts|Entra Agent ID}}, agent identity blueprints and conditional access for agents let you define permissions once per risk tier and enforce them at the identity layer.
- An agent registry, unified logging and a structured lifecycle from request to retirement turn shadow AI into governed, auditable agents that teams can deploy faster.

72550914.title: Work IQ: The New Intelligence Layer of Microsoft 365
72550914.key: work iq the new intelligence layer of microsoft 365
72550914.markup:
Work IQ turns your Microsoft 365 tenant from a filing cabinet into a reasoning system that sees every permission gap, bottleneck and broken process. This episode is for IT leaders and governance owners who need to prepare data, policies and management models before agents start acting on that intelligence, with a practical readiness check and a 90-day starting plan. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The productivity measurement crisis
- 06:20 – From the Microsoft Graph backbone to Work IQ
- 12:14 – Aggregation, permissions and data hygiene
- 26:46 – Inference and memory risks
- 33:19 – {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/agent-365/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=work-iq-the-new-intelligence-layer-of-microsoft-365|Agent 365}} and agent autonomy
- 36:51 – Why AI projects fail and the management model
- 46:49 – Governance framework and measuring intelligence
- 60:28 – The 2026 inflection point, readiness and the first 90 days

**Key takeaways**
- Work IQ adds a persistent context and memory layer on top of Microsoft Graph, turning {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/microsoft-365/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=work-iq-the-new-intelligence-layer-of-microsoft-365|Microsoft 365}} from a storage system into a reasoning system.
- Because Work IQ respects existing permissions, oversharing, stale sites and weak {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/sensitivity-labels/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=work-iq-the-new-intelligence-layer-of-microsoft-365|sensitivity labels}} become immediate risks, so data cleanup and governance must come before deployment.
- Measure decision speed, context reuse and outcome quality instead of activity, and start with one high-value workflow measured at 30, 60 and 90 days.

- 13:03 – The agent fabric and its economics
- 19:49 – Migration, deployment and optimization agents
- 29:46 – Observability, resiliency and troubleshooting agents
- 40:06 – Identity, orchestration and data governance
- 50:14 – Guardrails and outcomes
- 62:43 – Starting small and building the fabric

**Key takeaways**
- Cloud teams have more observability data than ever; the bottleneck is reasoning across fragmented tools, not visibility.
- Azure Copilot agents for migration, deployment, optimization, observability, resiliency and troubleshooting work best as a coordinated fabric with shared context.

**Worth quoting** “The real cost of manual cloud operations isn't the lack of information, it's the cost of interpretation, it's the cost of decision making” – Mirko Peters (01:11) “This is why you're perpetually reactive, not because your team isn't trying, but because your oversight model is asynchronous while your infrastructure is synchronous.” – Mirko Peters (08:33) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72550124.title: Dataverse MCP: The End of Custom Integration
72550124.key: dataverse mcp the end of custom integration
72550124.markup:
Every new AI tool still triggers another custom connector, and the maintenance and security debt keeps growing. This episode is for Power Platform architects, integration engineers and IT leaders who want to understand how Dataverse MCP changes enterprise integration. You learn where MCP saves time and tokens, where governance and security gaps remain, and how to plan a realistic migration. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why custom integration became the default
- 06:24 – What the Model Context Protocol is
- 09:18 – The Dataverse MCP connector and its security model
- 13:22 – Performance trade-offs and the economics of retiring connectors
- 20:20 – The governance gap: {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/dlp/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=dataverse-mcp-the-end-of-custom-integration|DLP}}, identity and attribution
- 28:29 – MCP as a new attack surface
- 32:51 – Hub and spoke architecture and Dataverse as context
- 44:45 – New roles, mistakes, maturity model and action plan

**Key takeaways**
- Custom connectors create compounding integration debt, while one governed MCP server per domain can serve many AI clients with the same security model and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/audit-logs/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=dataverse-mcp-the-end-of-custom-integration|audit trail}}.
- Classic DLP policies and audit logs do not yet see MCP servers or {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/ai-agent/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=dataverse-mcp-the-end-of-custom-integration|agent}} actions clearly, so advanced connector policies, Entra agent identities and interim controls such as approval workflows matter.
- Clean, business-readable Dataverse metadata and a governance-first design are prerequisites for MCP, because AI agents only understand what the schema and descriptions tell them.

**Explore more on M365.FM**

72665639.title: Building Enterprise AI Agents with Copilot Studio, Power Platform & AI Governance with Sailaja Mantripragada [MVP/MCT]
72665639.key: building enterprise ai agents with copilot studio power platform ai governance with sailaja mantripragada mvp mct
72665639.markup:
Artificial Intelligence is moving beyond simple chatbots and basic prompt engineering. Organizations around the world are now exploring how AI Agents can automate business processes, generate deliverables, reason through complex tasks, interact with enterprise systems, and transform the way work gets done.In {{link|https://www.m365.fm/building-enterprise-ai-agents-with-copilot-studio-power-platform-ai-governance-with-sailaja-mantr/|this episode}} of the M365 Podcast, Mirko Peters sits down with Sailaja Mantripragada, Microsoft Business Applications MVP, Microsoft Certified Trainer, Principal Cloud Architect, and Founder of Low Code Power. With more than twenty years of experience in the Microsoft ecosystem, Sailaja shares her journey from SharePoint development to {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-platform-simply-explained/|Power Platform}} architecture, enterprise AI strategy, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/categories/copilot-talk/|Copilot}} Studio, Agentic AI, and AI Governance.The conversation explores what separates real enterprise AI implementations from proof-of-concept demos, why governance has become one of the most important topics in modern AI adoption, and how organizations can successfully balance innovation, security, compliance, and scalability when building intelligent solutions.Whether you are a Power Platform developer, Microsoft 365 architect, AI strategist, business leader, or technology enthusiast, this episode provides practical insights into the future of enterprise AI and Microsoft's rapidly evolving ecosystem. **FROM SHAREPOINT TO AI GOVERNANCE** Sailaja's career spans more than two decades in the Microsoft technology landscape. Starting as a developer and SharePoint specialist, she witnessed Microsoft's evolution from a highly proprietary ecosystem into an open and collaborative platform embracing cloud technologies, low-code development, and artificial intelligence.One of the key themes throughout her journey has been governance. While technologies have changed dramatically over the years, the challenge of managing growth, scalability, adoption, and long-term maintainability has remained constant.During the discussion, Sailaja explains how organizations have moved from democratizing information through SharePoint to democratizing application development through Power Platform and now democratizing intelligence through Copilot and AI Agents. This progression is creating unprecedented opportunities while simultaneously introducing entirely new governance challenges. **WHY LOW-CODE IS RESHAPING ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT** Long before the term "low-code" became mainstream, Sailaja recognized a pattern across large enterprise projects. Organizations consistently preferred solutions built with out-of-the-box capabilities, reusable components, and business-focused outcomes instead of highly customized code that required extensive maintenance.This realization led her to specialize in low-code development years before Microsoft formally embraced the movement through Power Platform.The discussion explores how low-code development continues to evolve and why business users, citizen developers, and professional developers must increasingly collaborate rather than compete.Topics covered include:
- The rise of citizen development
- Business-first application design
- Power Apps and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-automate-simply-explained/|Power Automate}} adoption
- Enterprise scalability challenges
- The future of natural language development

Sailaja argues that successful organizations will empower citizen developers while simultaneously providing governance frameworks and architectural oversight to ensure long-term success. **THE CRITICAL ROLE OF AI GOVERNANCE** One of the most important themes throughout the episode is AI Governance.As organizations rush to deploy Copilot, AI Agents, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-platform-solutions/|Power Platform solutions}}, and generative AI experiences, many are discovering that years of unmanaged data, permissions, and legacy configurations are creating significant risks.Sailaja describes governance as the process of turning on the lights in rooms that organizations forgot existed.With AI systems now capable of discovering, analyzing, and retrieving information across multiple data sources, previously hidden security gaps, permission issues, and compliance risks become immediately visible.The conversation dives deep into:
- AI Governance frameworks
- Responsible AI implementation
- Data access management
- Security controls
- Compliance requirements
- Governance Centers of Excellence
- Enterprise AI oversight

Rather than acting as a barrier to innovation, governance should function as an enabler that helps organizations safely scale AI initiatives while maintaining trust and compliance. **BUILD FAST, GOVERN FASTER** One phrase appears repeatedly throughout the discussion:"Build Fast. Govern Faster."This philosophy forms the foundation of Sailaja's approach to enterprise AI adoption.Instead of treating governance as an afterthought, organizations should embed governance practices directly into the development lifecycle from day one.She explains how successful organizations create governance portals, approval workflows, audit trails, AI usage policies, and review processes before allowing large-scale AI development initiatives to take place.Key recommendations include:
- Establish AI governance policies early
- Create approval and review processes
- Train citizen developers
- Build AI Centers of Excellence
- Document business purpose and ownership
- Maintain visibility across AI solutions

This governance-first mindset helps prevent organizations from creating large numbers of uncontrolled AI agents and automation workflows that become difficult to manage over time. **COPILOT STUDIO AND THE FUTURE OF AI AGENTS** Copilot Studio has quickly become one of Microsoft's most strategic platforms for enterprise AI development.During the episode, Sailaja explains why Copilot Studio is far more than a chatbot builder. Instead, she describes it as the orchestration engine for modern AI solutions.Organizations can use Copilot Studio to coordinate workflows, connect enterprise systems, integrate AI services, manage agent interactions, and build sophisticated automation experiences that extend far beyond conversational interfaces.The discussion explores:
- Copilot Studio architecture
- Enterprise AI orchestration
- Agent development
- Workflow automation
- Business process integration
- AI-powered deliverables
- Multi-agent systems

As organizations mature their AI strategies, Copilot Studio increasingly becomes the central platform where business logic, AI reasoning, enterprise data, and automation capabilities converge. **UNDERSTANDING AGENTIC AI** Agentic AI is one of the hottest topics in the industry today, but it is also one of the most misunderstood.Sailaja provides a practical explanation of what separates a simple AI Agent from a true Agentic AI system.Rather than executing a single task, Agentic AI involves multiple agents working together, sharing context, making decisions, coordinating actions, and dynamically adapting to changing situations.The conversation explores how organizations are moving from prompt-based interactions toward complete business deliverables.Instead of asking AI a series of individual questions, users can increasingly provide a single business objective and allow multiple agents to collaborate behind the scenes to produce a finished outcome.Topics discussed include:
- AI Agents
- Agentic AI
- Reasoning systems
- Multi-agent orchestration
- Business deliverables
- Context engineering
- Enterprise workflows

This shift represents one of the biggest changes currently taking place in enterprise technology. **CONTEXT ENGINEERING IS THE NEW PROMPT ENGINEERING** While prompt engineering dominated early AI discussions, Sailaja believes the future belongs to context engineering.Organizations are beginning to realize that reusable prompts alone are not enough. High-quality AI outcomes depend on accurate context, trusted data, and business-specific knowledge.She introduces the concept of:
- Enterprise prompt libraries
- Department-specific context libraries
- Governance-approved AI instructions
- Business-aligned context management
- Organizational AI frameworks

The discussion highlights why context quality will become one of the most important differentiators between successful and unsuccessful AI deployments in the coming years. **MCP, GROUNDING, AND TRUSTED AI** As AI adoption accelerates, ensuring trustworthy outputs becomes increasingly important.Sailaja explains the growing importance of Model Context Protocol (MCP) and how it provides standardized access to enterprise data sources.The conversation explores how MCP contributes to:
- Data grounding
- Consistent access patterns
- Enterprise integrations
- Reduced hallucinations
- Better AI reliability
- Secure information retrieval

Grounding AI systems in trusted enterprise data helps organizations improve accuracy while maintaining confidence in AI-generated outcomes. Become a supporter of this podcast: {{link|https://www.spreaker.com/podcast/m365-fm-microsoft-365-azure-cloud-power-platform-ai--6704921/support?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss|https://www.spreaker.com/podcast/m365-fm-microsoft-365-azure-cloud-power-platform-ai--6704921/support}}.

72652352.title: The Terminal is No Longer for Commands: Building the Agentic Developer Stack
72652352.key: the terminal is no longer for commands building the agentic developer stack
72652352.markup:
AI made the editor smarter, but the real bottlenecks sit in the terminal, the pipeline and the review queue. This episode shows developers and engineering leaders how Copilot CLI, modernization, code review and coding agents form an agentic developer stack, and which context, guardrails and metrics make it work without creating new technical debt. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The structural flaw: smart editor, dumb execution layer
- 05:27 – Why the terminal became the center of gravity
- 07:45 – The four-layer agentic developer stack
- 15:43 – Validation and execution: code review and coding agents
- 25:04 – Context engineering and cross-model review
- 34:46 – Guardrails, bounded autonomy and self-healing agents
- 41:07 – Tool integration with {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/mcp/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-terminal-is-no-longer-for-commands-building-the-agentic-developer-stack|MCP}}, reasoning and latency
- 55:40 – Metrics, feedback loops, new roles and failure modes

**Key takeaways**
- The agentic developer stack has four connected layers: orchestration in Copilot CLI, transformation by modernization agents, validation by code review agents and execution by cloud coding agents.
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/ai-agent/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-terminal-is-no-longer-for-commands-building-the-agentic-developer-stack|Agent}} output quality depends more on context, tools and guardrails than on the model, so maintain living project memory such as architecture files, gotchas and ADRs.
- Measure throughput, quality, cycle time, developer satisfaction and technical debt, and keep humans responsible for policy, review and final decisions.

**Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/ai-agent/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-terminal-is-no-longer-for-commands-building-the-agentic-developer-stack|AI agent}} – the core distinction of the episode: agents pursue goals within policy, tools only respond
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/agentic-sdlc/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-terminal-is-no-longer-for-commands-building-the-agentic-developer-stack|Agentic SDLC}} – the four-layer stack of orchestration, transformation, validation and execution that structures the episode
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/mcp/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-terminal-is-no-longer-for-commands-building-the-agentic-developer-stack|Model Context Protocol (MCP)}} – the standard protocol that gives coding agents access to tests, logs, APIs and cloud tools
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/github-copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-terminal-is-no-longer-for-commands-building-the-agentic-developer-stack|GitHub Copilot}} – its CLI, code review and cloud coding agent serve as the concrete layers of the stack

72563849.title: Beyond the Prompt: Building the Security Agent Fabric

72563849.markup:
SOC analysts drown in alerts while MTTR dashboards look great and attackers stay hidden. This episode is for security leaders and architects who want to move from human middleware to a governed security agent fabric, with phishing triage, conditional access and multi-agent validation as concrete examples. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The human middleware problem
- 03:45 – The metrics trap: MTTR vs. outcomes
- 09:58 – Phishing and alert triage agents
- 21:27 – Conditional access optimization agent
- 24:49 – Multi-agent debate and validation
- 31:33 – Governing agents and the autonomy spectrum
- 46:13 – SOC roles, costs and trust
- 63:11 – Phased implementation and the agent fabric

**Key takeaways**
- Alert fatigue is a system design problem: agents should become the orchestration layer so humans supervise decisions instead of clicking through every alert.
- Dwell time and true positives are better SOC metrics than MTTR, and multi-agent validation cuts false positives more than bigger models do.
- Agents need their own identities, least privilege, guardrails, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/audit-logs/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=beyond-the-prompt-building-the-security-agent-fabric|audit trails}} and a phased rollout from assistive to semi-autonomous before they gain more autonomy.

**Worth quoting** “When a machine handles the triage, enrichment, and correlation, speed becomes cheap. What becomes expensive is accuracy. What becomes precious is the human time spent on the stuff that actually matters.” – Mirko Peters (06:26) “If an agent can disable user accounts, it's a system administrator. If an agent can isolate endpoints from your network, it's a security operator.” – Mirko Peters (31:39) **Explore more on M365.FM**
