This episode explains for architects and platform teams how Microsoft Rayfin turns the backend into governed code inside Microsoft Fabric, why that matters for AI agents, and how to migrate away from custom APIs step by step. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The middleware crisis
- 01:14 – Why custom APIs became a liability
- 07:26 – The agentic AI catalyst
- 10:33 – What Rayfin actually is
- 17:24 – Code-first governance
- 20:51 – Strangler fig and anti-corruption layer
- 32:53 – HorizonDB, observability and security
- 39:29 – Organization, cost and migration

**Key takeaways**
- Fragmented custom APIs scatter authentication, monitoring and governance across many systems, which makes them a growing liability, especially for {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/ai-agent/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-custom-apis-microsoft-refine-rayfin-as-a-backend-as-a-service-baas|AI agents}}.
- Rayfin defines the whole backend in code, deploys it into Microsoft Fabric and enforces access policies, masking and audit trails by default.
- Adopt it gradually with a pilot domain, a facade and an anti-corruption layer, backed by templates, a governance library and a governance board.

**Worth quoting** “If your first API uses OAuth and your second uses API keys, you haven't gained flexibility. You have created inconsistency, and that inconsistency is a massive security liability.” – Mirko Peters (02:23) “The real cost of your backend isn't the initial build. It is the maintenance burden that grows silently until you are spending half your engineering capacity just to keep the lights on.” – Mirko Peters (03:22) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72633268.title: What Enterprise Software Can Learn from Video Games with Sandra Kiel [MVP]
72633268.key: what enterprise software can learn from video games with sandra kiel mvp
72633268.markup:
Why do organizations spend millions on Microsoft 365, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-platform-simply-explained/|Power Platform}}, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/categories/copilot-talk/|Copilot}}, AI initiatives, and digital transformation projects only to struggle with user adoption? Why do employees often avoid business applications whenever possible while voluntarily spending hours inside video games?In {{link|https://www.m365.fm/what-enterprise-software-can-learn-from-video-games-with-sandra-kiel-mvp/|this episode}} of the M365 Show, Mirko Peters sits down with Microsoft MVP Sandra Kiel to explore one of the most overlooked topics in enterprise technology: what business software can learn from game design.Sandra brings a unique perspective to the conversation. After spending more than two decades working with enterprise software and large-scale SAP implementations, she transitioned into the Microsoft ecosystem and eventually discovered how gaming principles could transform learning, adoption, collaboration, and digital experiences. What started as a family Minecraft adventure during the pandemic evolved into a business focused on gamification, immersive learning environments, and user-centered digital experiences.The discussion explores why many enterprise applications fail to engage users, how organizations can improve AI adoption, and why understanding human behavior is often more important than implementing the latest technology. **FROM ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE TO MINECRAFT: SANDRA KIEL'S UNEXPECTED JOURNEY INTO GAMIFICATION** Sandra shares her fascinating journey from enterprise SAP consulting into the Microsoft ecosystem and eventually into game design. After experiencing burnout from organizational politics rather than technology itself, she discovered a completely different perspective on user engagement and learning.During the pandemic, a simple request from her children to play Minecraft together sparked a new understanding of how people learn, collaborate, solve problems, and develop skills. What began as a family gaming experience quickly evolved into experiments with virtual workshops, collaborative learning environments, and interactive training scenarios.That journey ultimately led to the creation of innovative learning experiences that combine Microsoft technologies with proven gaming principles. **WHY MOST BUSINESS APPLICATIONS FAIL TO ENGAGE USERS** One of the most powerful insights from this episode is that many organizations unknowingly pay employees to fight their software every day.Sandra explains that traditional enterprise applications often suffer from common design problems:
- Endless scrolling interfaces with little guidance
- Limited feedback when users complete actions
- Complex navigation that overwhelms users
- No visible sense of progress or achievement

In contrast, video games have spent decades perfecting onboarding, engagement, motivation, progression systems, and user experience design.Games consistently show users where they are, what they need to do next, and why their actions matter. Enterprise applications frequently fail to provide the same clarity.The result is lower adoption, reduced productivity, poor data quality, and frustrated employees. **HOW VIDEO GAME DESIGN PRINCIPLES CAN IMPROVE MICROSOFT 365, POWER PLATFORM, AND COPILOT ADOPTION** The conversation dives deep into the psychology behind successful game experiences and how these concepts can be applied to modern workplaces.According to Sandra, successful adoption programs should focus on proven engagement mechanisms including:
- Clear goals and visible progress indicators
- Personalized learning journeys
- Meaningful challenges and rewards
- Social collaboration and community participation

Rather than forcing users through generic training programs, organizations should create experiences that allow employees to explore, experiment, and learn through discovery.This approach is especially important for AI adoption, where behavioral change matters far more than traditional training. **THE REAL REASON COPILOT ADOPTION IS DIFFICULT** Many organizations assume Copilot adoption is primarily a training challenge. Sandra disagrees.She argues that AI adoption is fundamentally a behavior-change problem.Providing employees with prompt libraries and one-time training sessions rarely creates lasting habits. Instead, organizations need to create experiences that encourage experimentation, curiosity, and continuous learning.Drawing from gaming concepts such as Core Loops and Habit Loops, Sandra explains how successful adoption programs encourage users to repeatedly engage with AI tools until new behaviors become natural.The lesson is simple: people do not change behavior because they attended training. They change behavior because they repeatedly experience value. **WHAT {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-apps-simply-explained/|POWER APPS}} MAKERS CAN LEARN FROM VIDEO GAMES** For Power Apps developers, citizen developers, solution architects, and UX designers, Sandra shares several practical recommendations.The most important principle is orientation.Users should always understand:
- Where they are
- What they are trying to accomplish
- How much progress they have made
- What happens next

Instead of building endless forms and complex screens, developers should think like game designers by creating structured journeys with clear milestones and visible outcomes.Simple improvements such as progress indicators, chapter-based navigation, contextual feedback, and clear objectives can dramatically improve user adoption. **COMMUNITY BUILDING, MICROSOFT MVPS, AND THE POWER OF RECOGNITION** The discussion also explores why communities are such an essential part of successful technology ecosystems.Sandra highlights the Microsoft MVP community as an excellent example of gamification principles in action. Recognition, contribution, progression, visibility, and shared knowledge all contribute to creating an engaged and thriving ecosystem.Whether inside gaming communities, open-source projects, or Microsoft technology communities, people are motivated when their contributions matter and when they can see the impact of their work.The same principles apply inside organizations trying to drive adoption and change. **WOMEN IN TECH, VISIBILITY, AND BUILDING MORE INCLUSIVE COMMUNITIES** Sandra also shares her perspective on women in technology, public speaking, and community leadership.The conversation explores the importance of visibility, mentorship, representation, and creating safe environments where new voices can share knowledge and contribute to the community.Rather than focusing solely on speaking opportunities, Sandra emphasizes the importance of encouraging people to become knowledge sharers. By lowering barriers and actively supporting participation, organizations and event organizers can help create stronger and more diverse communities. **KEY TAKEAWAYS FROM THIS EPISODE** The biggest lesson from this conversation is that technology adoption is rarely a technology problem.It is a human problem.Organizations that successfully implement Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Copilot, AI solutions, and digital workplace initiatives will be the ones that understand motivation, engagement, feedback, learning, and user experience.Video game developers have spent decades mastering these concepts.The future of enterprise software may depend on how quickly organizations start learning from them. **CONNECT WITH SANDRA KIEL** If you enjoyed this episode, be sure to connect with Sandra Kiel through her Microsoft community channels, conference sessions, workshops, and social platforms. Her work at the intersection of gaming, Microsoft technologies, AI adoption, user experience, and digital transformation offers a unique perspective for anyone building the future workplace. **LISTEN, SUBSCRIBE, AND SHARE** If you enjoyed this episode of the M365 Show, subscribe on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, and your favorite podcast platform. Share the episode with colleagues, Microsoft professionals, Power Platform makers, UX designers, digital workplace leaders, and anyone responsible for driving technology adoption inside their organization.Because great technology is not just about features.It is about creating experiences people actually want to use. This episode is for intranet owners, SharePoint architects and digital workplace leads who want to replace page-view vanity metrics with real telemetry. - 47:00 – The optimization loop and Knowledge Agent
- 57:20 – AI-generated pages and self-optimizing intranets

**Key takeaways**
- Page views measure popularity, not usefulness; real intranet quality only shows up in behavioral signals like scroll depth, failed searches and rage clicks.
- Combining Microsoft Graph, SharePoint analytics, search logs and Microsoft Clarity turns isolated symptoms into a diagnosis and enables a continuous optimization loop.
- AI can analyze, generate and optimize SharePoint pages, but only on clean metadata and information architecture and with human approval, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/sensitivity-labels/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-end-of-static-sharepoint-why-ai-will-design-your-next-intranet|sensitivity labels}} and governance in place.

Someone whose job includes keeping the product healthy, not as an afterthought.” – Mirko Peters (07:25) “If your permissions are messy, AI can't safely retrieve information. Graph doesn't fix these problems. It makes them visible to systems that can. And that visibility is the first step toward automated optimization.” – Mirko Peters (20:59) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72542329.title: The Death of the Generalist Bot: Why Your Copilot Needs a Mixture of Experts
72542329.key: the death of the generalist bot why your copilot needs a mixture of experts
72542329.markup:
Most teams build one copilot on one big model and wonder why costs rise, answers blur and governance gets messy. This episode is for architects and AI platform owners on the Microsoft stack. It shows how to replace the generalist bot with a governed mixture of experts, with small-model routing, Copilot Studio and Foundry roles, escalation logic and Agent 365 governance. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why the generalist bot breaks at scale
- 04:12 – The cost model teams never map
- 07:52 – Why smaller models win more work
- 11:04 – What mixture of experts really means
- 14:34 – Copilot Studio as face, Foundry as brain
- 18:06 – Router first and expert domains
- 32:04 – Governance, Agent 365 and Azure Policy
- 59:25 – Build path, maturity and operating model

**Key takeaways**
- A single generalist copilot running every request on a premium model creates cost, quality and governance debt; a governed fabric of bounded experts fits enterprise work better.
- Make a cheap, structured router the first expert, use small models for routine traffic and escalate to premium reasoning or human review only on clear confidence, ambiguity and risk triggers.
- Let Copilot Studio own the user experience and Foundry own model control, and govern the fabric with {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/agent-365/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-generalist-bot-why-your-copilot-needs-a-mixture-of-experts|Agent 365}}, Azure Policy model allow lists, traces and named owners.

**Worth quoting** “broad coverage is not the same as operational fitness. A system that can attempt every task is not a system that should own every task” – Mirko Peters (01:29) “Even if your own workload lands differently, the direction is clear. Better routing changes the bill, more than endless prompt tuning on the wrong model.” – Mirko Peters (06:44) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72539777.title: Latency vs. Logic: Engineering High-Stakes Hybrid Events in M365
72539777.key: latency vs logic engineering high stakes hybrid events in m365
72539777.markup:
Immersive team events in Microsoft Teams often fail not because of the 3D technology but because of network latency, unequal hardware and missing orchestration. This episode shows Microsoft 365 admins and event organizers how to engineer latency and logic together, from network and Quest security checks to agenda design and Power BI measurement. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Anatomy of a failed immersive event
- 03:53 – From Mesh to Teams immersive
- 06:20 – Infrastructure reality check
- 09:28 – Network architecture and latency budgets
- 22:16 – Hardware parity, spatial audio and GPUs
- 40:32 – The logic layer and multi-user state
- 56:09 – Conditional access and Quest security
- 60:49 – Agenda, checklist and measurement

**Key takeaways**
- Microsoft Mesh now lives inside Teams as immersive spaces and events, so it inherits Teams licensing, identity, compliance and network paths, along with their limitations such as no web, mobile, VDI, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/teams-rooms/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=latency-vs-logic-engineering-high-stakes-hybrid-events-in-m365|Teams Rooms}} or dial-in support.
- Treat immersive events as systems engineering: audit network paths, split tunneling and QoS, test hardware and Quest sign-in under conditional access, and keep a standard Teams meeting as a fallback.
- Spend more effort on logic than on decoration, using server-mediated, collaborative activities, a 60-minute agenda and Power Platform-based registration and measurement.

**Worth quoting** “Most organizations invest 90% of their effort in visual customization and 10% in logical orchestration. The successful ones flip that ratio. They spend more time designing the flow of the event than decorating the space” – Mirko Peters (42:23) “Users are more tolerant of latency when visual feedback is continuous even if slightly delayed. They're less tolerant when latency is inconsistent.” – Mirko Peters (19:24) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72541178.title: Private RAG Isn't Enough: The Missing Layer Between Data Sovereignty and Data Security
72541178.key: private rag isn t enough the missing layer between data sovereignty and data security
72541178.markup:
Private RAG projects focus on where data lives, but often lose the permissions that decided who could see it. This episode is for CISOs, architects and engineers building AI retrieval on SharePoint and Microsoft 365 data, and explains how permission-aware retrieval, scoped identity and policy engines stop a knowledge system from becoming an insider data leak. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why private RAG is about location, not access
- 04:01 – Three misconceptions about private RAG
- 06:53 – What happens when documents leave SharePoint
- 10:20 – ACL metadata extraction and authorization before retrieval
- 17:13 – The five-agent retrieval model and identity propagation
- 28:07 – Policy decision points and multi-tenant leakage
- 35:01 – Shadow AI, zero trust and detection
- 44:46 – Cost, tooling and where permission-aware RAG is heading

**Key takeaways**
- Keeping data in a sovereign region does not protect it: if SharePoint permissions are lost during extraction, a RAG index exposes documents to anyone who can query it.
- Capture ACLs as Entra ID-based metadata at ingestion and filter by user and group before retrieval, for example with {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-ai-search/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=private-rag-isnt-enough-the-missing-layer-between-data-sovereignty-and-data-security|Azure AI Search}}, instead of filtering afterwards or relying on the prompt.
- Separate responsibilities across agents, use scoped tokens via OAuth 2.0 token exchange and a deterministic policy decision point, and monitor retrieval behavior with zero trust at every hop.

**Worth quoting** “If you extract documents from SharePoint to build a perfect retrieval system, but lose the permission model that SharePoint was enforcing, what have you actually built?” – Mirko Peters (00:50) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/private-rag-isnt-enough-the-missing-layer-between-data-sovereignty-and-data-security/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=private-rag-isnt-enough-the-missing-layer-between-data-sovereignty-and-data-security|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, key quotes and an FAQ on permission-aware RAG
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/rag/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=private-rag-isnt-enough-the-missing-layer-between-data-sovereignty-and-data-security|Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)}} – the retrieval pattern whose private deployments lose SharePoint permissions during extraction, chunking and embedding
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/sharepoint/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=private-rag-isnt-enough-the-missing-layer-between-data-sovereignty-and-data-security|SharePoint}} – the source system whose layered site, library, folder and item permissions get lost during RAG ingestion
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/zero-trust/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=private-rag-isnt-enough-the-missing-layer-between-data-sovereignty-and-data-security|Zero Trust}} – the never-trust, always-verify model applied to every agent hop with scoped tokens and mutual TLS

72535434.key: your sharepoint data is a liability fixing the metadata gap
72535434.markup:
Most SharePoint files carry no business metadata, leaving organizations unable to find contracts, enforce retention or trust Copilot answers. This episode is for SharePoint architects, compliance teams and Microsoft 365 admins who want to close the metadata gap with a governed taxonomy, document processing models, autofill columns and agents. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why SharePoint data without metadata is a liability
- 08:17 – The metadata foundation: term sets, columns and content types
- 14:19 – Governance, compliance and Copilot readiness
- 20:33 – What intelligent document processing means
- 28:01 – Syntex, SharePoint Premium and Document Processing
- 34:18 – Model types: structured, freeform and unstructured
- 40:36 – Agents, skills, autofill and building custom models
- 69:30 – From metadata to governed action and scaling

**Key takeaways**
- The real SharePoint problem is not storage but missing business metadata, which breaks search, retention, DLP, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/ediscovery/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=your-sharepoint-data-is-a-liability-fixing-the-metadata-gap|eDiscovery}} and Copilot grounding.
- Design the taxonomy first, with term sets, site columns and content types, because document processing models need a target vocabulary to populate.
- Syntex capabilities now live on as document processing and AI in SharePoint, so inventory existing models, govern skills and autofill carefully, and connect extracted metadata to {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/purview/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=your-sharepoint-data-is-a-liability-fixing-the-metadata-gap|Purview}} retention and sensitivity labels.

72538680.title: Securing Identities at Scale: Conditional Access, Azure Security & Infrastructure as Code with Jonathan Hope [MVP]
72538680.key: securing identities at scale conditional access azure security infrastructure as code with jonathan hope mvp
72538680.markup:
Security defaults and one-time setups leave identities exposed while attackers use phishing, password reset abuse and guest accounts to get in. This episode is for Microsoft 365 and Azure admins, architects and MSPs who need to secure identities at scale. Microsoft MVP Jonathan Hope shares his foundation Conditional Access policies and why Bicep and policy as code make security repeatable. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Welcome and Jonathan Hope's path from VMware to Azure
- 02:47 – Identity as the new perimeter
- 09:44 – How attackers target identities
- 15:18 – Active Directory, hybrid identity and cloud-first groups
- 19:28 – Conditional Access and the six foundation policies
- 26:25 – AI, Zero Trust and Azure versus identity security
- 34:46 – Infrastructure as code with Bicep
- 45:11 – Policy as code, the security roadmap and quick-fire round

**Key takeaways**
- Identity is the new perimeter, and Conditional Access acts as a real-time firewall that evaluates every access request using signals from {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/intune/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=securing-identities-at-scale-conditional-access-azure-security-infrastructure-as-code-with-jonathan-hope|Intune}}, Defender and Purview.
- A small set of foundation policies such as MFA for all users, stronger methods for admins, blocking device code flow and legacy authentication, and country controls stops most low-hanging attacks.
- Infrastructure as code with Bicep and policy as code turn security configurations into repeatable, documented standards that keep up with constant portal changes.

**Worth quoting** “I mean, you wouldn't put a server in place and then rely on the Comcast modem from your internet service provider. You would get a firewall, right? You would be precise about the technology.” – Jonathan Hope (05:21) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72534214.title: Stop Leaking Data: How to Run Local Llama on Your SharePoint Files
72534214.key: stop leaking data how to run local llama on your sharepoint files
72534214.markup:
Connecting cloud AI to SharePoint can expose contracts, HR files and board memos to infrastructure and legal regimes you do not control. This episode is for Microsoft 365 architects and security teams who need private AI, and it walks through a seven-layer, air-gapped RAG architecture with local Llama, Ollama and Qdrant that respects SharePoint permissions. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Sovereign intelligence, not sovereign cloud
- 04:39 – The air-gapped alternative and the seven-layer stack
- 07:38 – Why retrieval is essential and SharePoint as the content backbone
- 14:20 – Local vs. cloud LLMs, vector databases and embeddings
- 23:55 – Ingestion, extraction and chunking strategy for SharePoint documents
- 39:33 – Configuring Qdrant and running Llama locally with Ollama
- 58:21 – Query interface, permission tiers and access control
- 64:49 – Scaling, model evolution and the complete blueprint

**Key takeaways**
- Sending SharePoint content to cloud AI moves it into logs and legal jurisdictions you do not control, while a local stack with Llama, a vector database and on-premises embeddings keeps every query inside your perimeter.
- Retrieval quality depends mostly on chunking: use heading-aware chunks for Word, page-aware chunks for PDFs, row groups with headers for Excel and slide-level chunks for PowerPoint, and keep source metadata on every chunk for citations.
- Mirror SharePoint permissions exactly by tagging every vector with a permission tier at ingestion and filtering by the user's {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=stop-leaking-data-how-to-run-local-llama-on-your-sharepoint-files|Entra ID}} groups at query time, backed by local audit logs and regular permission reconciliation.

**Explore more on M365.FM**

- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/sharepoint/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=stop-leaking-data-how-to-run-local-llama-on-your-sharepoint-files|SharePoint}} – the document source the local RAG pipeline ingests, keeping its permissions and retention rules
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/rag/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=stop-leaking-data-how-to-run-local-llama-on-your-sharepoint-files|Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)}} – the retrieval pattern that grounds local Llama answers in chunks from SharePoint documents

AI is reshaping hiring, and many tech professionals feel the job market is against them. In this conversation, recruiter and career coach Sarah Jones explains what recruiters and ATS systems look for, how to build a personal brand on LinkedIn without burning out, and what it takes to move into freelancing in the Microsoft ecosystem. **In this episode**

I think you're going to have to be able to articulate your value in your role more” – Sarah Jones (11:26) “personal brand is about trust, but having a platform to speak on, and then also demonstrate what problems you can solve for people in public.” – Sarah Jones (25:18) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72533680.title: The Architect's Guide to MCP: Building the Connectivity Layer for Microsoft AI Agents
72533680.key: the architect s guide to mcp building the connectivity layer for microsoft ai agents
72533680.markup:
Most AI pilots stall not because the model is weak but because agents cannot reach the systems that hold the data. This episode gives Microsoft architects a practical guide to the Model Context Protocol, from the wire protocol and C# SDK to Azure deployment, Copilot Studio, Work IQ, A2A and agent identity, ending with a 90-day roadmap to production. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The connectivity crisis for AI agents
- 02:46 – What MCP is and why JSON-RPC
- 13:35 – MCP architecture deep dive: handshake and primitives
- 21:55 – Building your first MCP server with the C# SDK
- 30:45 – Transports and Azure deployment patterns
- 45:33 – Copilot Studio and Work IQ as MCP servers
- 55:42 – A2A orchestration and agent security with Entra Agent ID
- 65:37 – Reference architecture and the 90-day roadmap

**Key takeaways**
- MCP sits above {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/graph/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-architects-guide-to-mcp-building-the-connectivity-layer-for-microsoft-ai-agents|Microsoft Graph}}, REST APIs and connectors as a standard discovery and capability layer, so one MCP server can serve every agent in the organization.
- Use STDIO only for local development and streamable HTTP behind Azure API Management with Entra authentication for production; SSE is deprecated.
- Combine MCP for tools with A2A for agent collaboration, and secure every agent with Entra Agent ID, Conditional Access and Agent 365 from day one.

**Worth quoting** “The organizations that are winning with AI right now aren't the ones with the best models. They are the ones with the best connectivity layer.” – Mirko Peters (02:29) “MCP doesn't replace Microsoft Graph. It doesn't replace your REST APIs. It doesn't replace your custom connectors. It sits above them. MCP is the translation layer.” – Mirko Peters (07:47) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/the-architects-guide-to-mcp-building-the-connectivity-layer-for-microsoft-ai-agents/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-architects-guide-to-mcp-building-the-connectivity-layer-for-microsoft-ai-agents|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, quotes, FAQ and the 90-day MCP roadmap

72455506.title: From Project Online to AI-Powered Project Delivery: The Evolution of Dynamics 365 Project Operations with Joe Griffin [MVP]
72455506.key: from project online to ai powered project delivery the evolution of dynamics 365 project operations with joe griffin mvp
72455506.markup:
In this insightful episode of the M365 Podcast, host Mirko Peters welcomes Joe Griffin, Microsoft MVP, CEO of proMX UK, Microsoft Certified Trainer, and one of the most recognized experts in Dynamics 365 Project Operations. With more than 40 Microsoft certifications covering Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Azure, Artificial Intelligence, and the broader Microsoft Cloud ecosystem, Joe brings a unique blend of technical expertise, business leadership, and real-world implementation experience.The conversation explores one of the most important transitions currently happening in the Microsoft project management landscape: the retirement of Microsoft Project Online and the growing adoption of Dynamics 365 Project Operations. Joe explains why organizations should start preparing now, what migration paths are available, and how businesses can use this moment as an opportunity to modernize not only their technology stack but also their project delivery processes. **UNDERSTANDING DYNAMICS 365 PROJECT OPERATIONS** Joe provides a comprehensive overview of Dynamics 365 Project Operations and explains why it has become a strategic platform for project-based organizations. Unlike traditional project management tools that focus solely on task management and scheduling, Project Operations combines project planning, resource allocation, budgeting, financial management, time tracking, expense management, invoicing, and AI-driven insights into a single solution built on Microsoft Dataverse.The discussion highlights how organizations can gain end-to-end visibility across project lifecycles while improving resource utilization and financial performance. Joe also explains how Project Operations leverages familiar Microsoft technologies such as Planner, Power Platform, and Dataverse to create a connected and scalable project management environment. **KEY TAKEAWAYS:**
- What Dynamics 365 Project Operations actually does
- Who should consider adopting the platform
- How it differs from traditional project management tools
- Why professional services organizations benefit the most
- The role of Dataverse and Power Platform

**PROJECT ONLINE RETIREMENT AND MIGRATION STRATEGIES** A major focus of the episode is Microsoft's planned retirement of Project Online. Joe explains what the announcement means for existing customers and outlines the options available for organizations currently relying on Project Online for project planning and portfolio management.Drawing from real-world migration projects, Joe shares practical advice on preparing data, simplifying project structures, and avoiding common migration pitfalls. He also discusses the importance of reviewing legacy processes and using the migration as an opportunity to modernize project management practices.The conversation dives into technical considerations such as Project Desktop files, Scheduler APIs, resource mapping, testing environments, and large-scale migration automation. **MIGRATION TOPICS COVERED:**
- Project Online retirement implications
- Migration planning and assessment
- Common data migration challenges
- Managing complex project portfolios
- Best practices for successful adoption

**HOW AI IS CHANGING PROJECT MANAGEMENT** Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming business applications, and Dynamics 365 Project Operations is no exception. Joe explores how Microsoft is embedding AI across the platform and shares practical examples of AI-powered capabilities available today.One particularly interesting example is the Time Entry Agent, which can automatically generate draft timesheets based on calendars, resource assignments, and previous activities. Instead of chasing employees for timesheet submissions, organizations can leverage AI to automate much of the process while maintaining human oversight.The discussion also covers AI-generated project status reports, intelligent resource recommendations, project risk identification, and the future potential of autonomous project management capabilities. **AI IN PROJECT OPERATIONS:**
- Automated time entry generation
- AI-powered status reporting
- Intelligent resource recommendations
- Risk detection and forecasting
- Future project management {{link|https://www.m365.fm/categories/copilot-talk/|agents}}

**POWER PLATFORM AND AZURE INTEGRATION** Joe explains why the real power of Dynamics 365 Project Operations comes from its integration with the wider Microsoft ecosystem. Because the platform is built on Dataverse, organizations can extend functionality using Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, Power Pages, and Azure services.Listeners will learn how companies can create custom project experiences, automate business processes, build advanced reporting solutions, and integrate Project Operations with external ERP systems. Joe also discusses how {{link|https://www.m365.fm/azure-service-bus-simply-explained/|Azure Service Bus}}, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/azure-functions-simply-explained/|Azure Functions}}, and modern integration architectures help organizations scale complex project environments.The episode provides valuable guidance for solution architects and technical leaders looking to design enterprise-grade project management solutions that remain scalable and maintainable over time. **ARCHITECTURE AND EXTENSIBILITY TOPICS:**
- Power Apps customization strategies
- Power Automate workflows
- Power BI reporting and analytics
- Azure integration patterns
- Enterprise architecture best practices

**THE ROLE OF {{link|https://www.m365.fm/microsoft-fabric-simply-explained/|MICROSOFT FABRIC}} AND AI FOUNDRY** Looking ahead, the conversation explores emerging technologies such as Microsoft Fabric and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/azure-ai-foundry-simply-explained/|Azure AI Foundry}}. Joe explains how Fabric can serve as a centralized data foundation for AI initiatives by bringing together information from Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and other business systems.The discussion highlights how organizations that establish strong data foundations today will be better positioned to take advantage of future AI capabilities. Joe also shares his perspective on AI Foundry, model selection, fine-tuning opportunities, and the growing importance of enterprise-ready AI governance. 72330537.title: Indirect Injection: The Silent Killer of Enterprise AI
72330537.key: indirect injection the silent killer of enterprise ai
72330537.markup:
Your Microsoft 365 Copilot reads SharePoint pages, emails and Teams chats that may hide instructions an attacker planted there. This episode explains for security and IT leaders why indirect prompt injection is an architectural flaw of RAG and how red teaming, dual LLM verification and zero-trust prompting close the gap. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – RAG turns data into code
- 06:22 – Why system instructions fail
- 17:38 – Weaponizing the data source
- 23:43 – The sleeper agent problem
- 28:43 – Real attack surfaces in {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/microsoft-365/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=indirect-injection-the-silent-killer-of-enterprise-ai|Microsoft 365}}
- 51:54 – Red teaming your own Copilot
- 62:11 – CaMeL and dual LLM verification
- 68:39 – Zero-trust prompting and the 2026 checklist

**Key takeaways**
- In RAG-based copilots every retrieved document becomes part of the prompt, so hidden text in {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/sharepoint/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=indirect-injection-the-silent-killer-of-enterprise-ai|SharePoint}}, email or Teams content can act as instructions.
- Access controls and system prompts do not stop indirect prompt injection; defenses must be architectural, such as dual LLM verification with a non-LLM controller.
- Zero-trust prompting, continuous red teaming and basic data hygiene of the retrieval corpus are needed before scaling Copilot beyond pilots.

**Worth quoting** “Access controls determine which data can be retrieved, prompt injection determines how that data is interpreted, and how the model behaves once it sees that data.” – Mirko Peters (03:27) “Your system prompt isn't a security boundary. It is a string of text that competes with every other string of text in the context window for the model's attention.” – Mirko Peters (44:41) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/indirect-injection-the-silent-killer-of-enterprise-ai/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=indirect-injection-the-silent-killer-of-enterprise-ai|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, quotes and a FAQ on indirect prompt injection
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/prompt-injection/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=indirect-injection-the-silent-killer-of-enterprise-ai|Prompt injection}} – the attack class at the center of the episode, listed as LLM01 by OWASP
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/rag/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=indirect-injection-the-silent-killer-of-enterprise-ai|Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)}} – the retrieval pattern that makes every retrieved document part of the model's prompt
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=indirect-injection-the-silent-killer-of-enterprise-ai|Microsoft 365 Copilot}} – the RAG-based assistant whose access to SharePoint, Outlook and Teams content forms the attack surface
- Related episode: {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/private-rag-isnt-enough-the-missing-layer-between-data-sovereignty-and-data-security/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=indirect-injection-the-silent-killer-of-enterprise-ai|Private RAG Isn't Enough: The Missing Layer Between Data Sovereignty and Data Security}}

72436166.title: From SharePoint Developer to Power Platform Architect: Building Secure and Scalable Solutions with Michel Mendes [MVP]
72436166.key: from sharepoint developer to power platform architect building secure and scalable solutions with michel mendes mvp
72436166.markup:
Low-code makes it easy to build apps and portals, and just as easy to expose data to the world by accident. In this conversation, Microsoft MVP Michel Mendes shares his path from SharePoint developer to Power Platform architect and explains how makers and architects can build Power Pages and Power Apps solutions that are secure, scalable and maintainable. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – From Java student in Brazil to SharePoint developer
- 03:44 – Configuration first: developer skills in a low-code world
- 05:39 – AI and the shift to code apps
- 07:38 – Citizen development and successful Power Platform projects
- 14:15 – Dataverse and Power Pages for external users
- 20:29 – How Power Pages evolved: solutions, server logic and SPA sites
- 24:11 – Power Pages security: Web API, table and column permissions
- 33:08 – AI in daily work, community and career advice

**Key takeaways**
- Start with out-of-the-box configuration and move to pro-code only when low-code is not enough, while keeping Dataverse security and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/governance/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=from-sharepoint-developer-to-power-platform-architect-building-secure-and-scalable-solutions-with-michel-mendes-mvp|governance}} in place.
- Use Power Pages for external users on top of Dataverse, and secure the Web API with enabled fields, table permissions and column permissions instead of hiding data in the client.
- AI speeds up prototypes and bug fixes, but developers remain responsible for review, security audits and spending tokens only where they create real impact.

**Worth quoting** “my mentors at that point, they taught me like, hey, you need to think first, and like, does the feature exist? Can you do it with configuration first? If you can't, then we go to Procode Approaches.” – Michel Mendes (04:23) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72327574.title: STOP BUILDING SILOED AGENTS: The Logic App Nervous System
72327574.key: stop building siloed agents the logic app nervous system
72327574.markup:
Organizations are deploying copilots and bots that each wire directly into their own APIs, credentials and logic, and the result breaks as soon as processes span systems and tenants. This episode is for architects and Microsoft 365 and Azure teams who want to turn siloed agents into an orchestrated system with Azure Logic Apps, custom connectors and secretless identity. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The chatbot mirage and point-to-point integrations
- 05:07 – Cross-tenant reality and the stateful gap
- 08:41 – {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-logic-apps/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=stop-building-siloed-agents-the-logic-app-nervous-system|Logic Apps}} as the nervous system: Standard vs. Consumption
- 14:41 – Connectors and orchestrator-first architecture
- 18:33 – Identity: managed identities and workload identity federation
- 25:30 – Error handling and human-on-the-loop governance
- 30:10 – A cross-tenant scenario, agent loop and custom connectors
- 52:10 – Anti-patterns, roadmap, objections and economics

**Key takeaways**
- Agents should reason but not execute alone: route them through an orchestrator that owns state, business rules, error handling and the audit trail instead of wiring each bot to every API.
- Azure Logic Apps Standard is the orchestration layer of choice for enterprise agents, combining stateful and stateless workflows, custom connectors as contracts and the {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/agent-loop/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=stop-building-siloed-agents-the-logic-app-nervous-system|agent loop}} action.
- Use managed identities inside a tenant and workload identity federation across tenants so that no client secrets live in the agent layer, then roll out in phases starting with one painful process.

- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-logic-apps/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=stop-building-siloed-agents-the-logic-app-nervous-system|Azure Logic Apps}} – the orchestration layer, ideally Standard, that owns state, connectors, identity and error handling for agents

72435214.title: Building Multi-Agent AI Systems with Copilot Studio: From Ideas to Intelligent Automation with David Lorenzo Lopez  [MVP]

72435214.markup:
Impressive AI demos are easy, but turning agents into reliable business automation is hard. In this interview, Microsoft MVP David Lorenzo Lopez explains to makers, developers and architects how multi-agent systems work in Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry and the Microsoft Agent Framework. You learn when to use which platform, where humans must stay in the loop and how to keep cost and governance under control. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Introducing David Lorenzo Lopez and his background
- 03:12 – The GPT moment and demos versus real business value
- 05:21 – What multi-agent systems are: from monolith to microservices
- 10:41 – Orchestration, agent collaboration and human approval
- 18:10 – Building in Copilot Studio and Foundry with agent flows and workflows
- 24:35 – Starting customer projects and EU AI Act compliance
- 31:00 – Copilot Studio vs. Foundry and the Microsoft Agent Framework
- 39:33 – FinOps, Agent 365 governance and quick-fire round

**Key takeaways**
- Multi-agent systems split one overloaded agent into specialized agents coordinated by an orchestrator, similar to the move from monoliths to microservices, which makes them easier to test and reuse.
- Choose Copilot Studio, Foundry low-code or the Microsoft Agent Framework based on licensing, data location, performance and customization needs, and keep critical operations behind human approval.
- Not every {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/automation/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=building-multi-agent-ai-systems-with-copilot-studio-from-ideas-to-intelligent-automation-with-david-lorenzo-lopez-mvp|automation}} needs AI; deterministic agent flows with AI only at specific steps, careful cost estimation and central governance with Agent 365 make agent projects deliver real value.

72326685.title: The Rise of Private LoRA: Architecting Secure AI on Proprietary Data
72326685.key: the rise of private lora architecting secure ai on proprietary data
72326685.markup:
Employees are pasting proprietary data into public AI tools, and regulations like the EU AI Act and GDPR are tightening the walls around where AI may run. This episode is for architects and IT leaders in Microsoft-centric enterprises who need AI that stays inside their boundary. Learn how private LoRA adapters, quantization and federated training deliver specialized, governable AI at a fraction of the cost. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Shadow AI and the sovereignty gap
- 08:56 – The regulatory walls are closing
- 22:00 – How LoRA and quantization work
- 37:44 – Adapter libraries and modular AI
- 42:57 – Building the private intelligence vault
- 50:35 – Benchmarks and ROI
- 64:34 – Federated LoRA and the collaboration paradox
- 72:47 – Your model zoo roadmap

**Key takeaways**
- Shadow AI use of public chatbots leaks proprietary context that Microsoft 365 Copilot's tenant protections do not cover, creating a sovereignty gap that is an architecture problem rather than a compliance one.
- LoRA adapters on frozen open-weight base models, combined with quantization, make private fine-tuning feasible on a single GPU and let one base model serve a governed library of department-specific specialists.
- Start with one high-volume, sensitive, narrow task inside your existing Azure boundary, prove it with A/B tests, then grow a governed model zoo integrated with Power Platform, Azure ML and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-rise-of-private-lora-architecting-secure-ai-on-proprietary-data|Entra ID}}.

**Worth quoting** “Centralized LLMs are outsourced intelligence. You rent capability but you surrender control. You get access to frontier reasoning but you give away proprietary context in exchange.” – Mirko Peters (07:43) “You only need to validate the small adapter you trained on top of it. The base model is a commodity. The adapter is your proprietary value.” – Mirko Peters (25:59) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/the-rise-of-private-lora-architecting-secure-ai-on-proprietary-data/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-rise-of-private-lora-architecting-secure-ai-on-proprietary-data|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, quotes and FAQ on private LoRA architecture
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-rise-of-private-lora-architecting-secure-ai-on-proprietary-data|Microsoft 365 Copilot}} – protects prompts at tenant level but cannot cover employees pasting data into public chatbots
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/eu-ai-act/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-rise-of-private-lora-architecting-secure-ai-on-proprietary-data|EU AI Act}} – its August 2026 high-risk deadline is one of the regulatory walls pushing AI inside the boundary

72325440.title: The Death of the Dropdown: Why Manual Tagging is Killing Your Governance
72325440.key: the death of the dropdown why manual tagging is killing your governance
72325440.markup:
If your Microsoft 365 governance still depends on users picking values from dropdowns, most of your content is probably untagged and invisible. This episode is for governance, compliance and SharePoint architects, and shows how Graph-driven middleware can classify and label content automatically so search, DLP and Copilot work on reliable metadata. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The manual metadata crisis
- 07:51 – Why dropdowns are a design failure
- 15:25 – Microsoft Graph as the organizational nervous system
- 23:57 – Architecting the middleware layer
- 31:46 – Dynamic property injection with schema extensions
- 37:22 – What it looks like in practice
- 43:48 – Governance at the point of action and compliance
- 59:29 – The search and AI payoff and building your roadmap

**Key takeaways**
- Manual dropdown tagging cannot scale with hybrid work and content volume, so untagged files become dark data that search, compliance tools and AI agents cannot use.
- Event-driven middleware on {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-functions/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-dropdown-why-manual-tagging-is-killing-your-governance|Azure Functions}} can query Microsoft Graph for context, write schema extension properties and apply Purview sensitivity labels at the moment content is created.
- Roll out in phases (audit, a small taxonomy, a single-team pilot, scale, optimize) and keep humans in the loop for low-confidence and high-risk classifications.

**Worth quoting** “If tagging a file takes 30 seconds, and the user doesn't personally benefit from the metadata, they will skip it. And if skipping is faster than doing it, skipping becomes the default behavior.” – Mirko Peters (10:17) “Manual tagging asks the user to declare what a file is. Graph-based governance observes what the file actually is in the context of the organization.” – Mirko Peters (16:02) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/the-death-of-the-dropdown-why-manual-tagging-is-killing-your-governance/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-dropdown-why-manual-tagging-is-killing-your-governance|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, key quotes and an FAQ on automated tagging
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/graph/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-dropdown-why-manual-tagging-is-killing-your-governance|Microsoft Graph}} – the source of context signals the middleware queries to derive metadata instead of asking users
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/governance/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-dropdown-why-manual-tagging-is-killing-your-governance|Governance}} – the episode's core subject, shifting from user tagging and cleanup to enforcement at creation
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/purview/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-death-of-the-dropdown-why-manual-tagging-is-killing-your-governance|Microsoft Purview}} – supplies classifiers and sensitive information types the middleware calls to label files at ingestion

72324407.title: Cryptographic Agility: The Only Defense Against Quantum
72324407.key: cryptographic agility the only defense against quantum
72324407.markup:
Quantum computers will break RSA and ECC, and attackers are already storing your encrypted traffic to decrypt it later. This episode is for security architects and Microsoft 365 and Azure administrators who need a realistic post-quantum plan. You will learn why cryptographic agility, not a single algorithm choice, decides whether your organization survives the transition. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why Encryption Will Become Obsolete
- 01:28 – Harvest Now, Decrypt Later
- 15:15 – The New Math: Lattice-Based Algorithms
- 27:13 – Performance Reality Check
- 38:22 – Hidden Cryptographic Dependencies
- 45:59 – The Agility Architecture
- 64:11 – PQC in the Microsoft Stack
- 72:34 – The {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/governance/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=cryptographic-agility-the-only-defense-against-quantum|Governance}} Playbook

**Key takeaways**
- Adversaries are already harvesting encrypted traffic, so data that must stay confidential for decades is at risk today, long before a quantum computer exists.
- The real weakness is rigid, hard-coded cryptography; modularity, API abstraction, policy separation and hybrid key exchange make algorithm changes survivable.
- Start with governance and a continuous cryptographic inventory, then use what Microsoft already ships (SymCrypt, AD CS ML-DSA, {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-key-vault/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=cryptographic-agility-the-only-defense-against-quantum|Key Vault}} previews, Edge defaults) for phased PQC adoption.

**Worth quoting** “Quantum computing merely accelerates the need for cryptographic agility that's already apparent from past algorithm deprecations and protocol shifts.” – Mirko Peters (13:39) “Without continuous discovery, crypto agility is a slogan. You can't be agile if you don't know where the crypto is.” – Mirko Peters (41:08) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/cryptographic-agility-the-only-defense-against-quantum/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=cryptographic-agility-the-only-defense-against-quantum|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, quotes and FAQ on post-quantum readiness
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-key-vault/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=cryptographic-agility-the-only-defense-against-quantum|Azure Key Vault}} – offers ML-KEM and ML-DSA key types in preview with automated key rotation for PQC testing
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/entra-id/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=cryptographic-agility-the-only-defense-against-quantum|Microsoft Entra ID}} – signs access tokens and is working on post-quantum protection for identity tokens and federation
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/governance/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=cryptographic-agility-the-only-defense-against-quantum|Governance}} – the playbook of executive sponsorship, continuous inventory and risk-based prioritization that makes agility last

72432683.title: Microsoft Purview in the Age of AI: Securing Copilot with Peter Rising [Microsoft]
72432683.key: microsoft purview in the age of ai securing copilot with peter rising microsoft
72432683.markup:
Copilot and AI agents can reach any data your permissions allow, which turns weak data governance into a real exposure risk. In this interview, Microsoft partner solution architect Peter Rising explains to IT, security and compliance leaders how Purview, Zero Trust and defense in depth make AI adoption safe. You get a practical starting point covering sensitivity labels, DLP, retention and oversharing controls. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Introduction and Peter's career journey
- 04:09 – Partner role and shared responsibility
- 07:14 – How AI changed the security conversation
- 09:36 – Zero Trust principles in practice
- 18:28 – Purview core features and evolution
- 28:41 – Copilot governance and oversharing
- 40:37 – Agents and the future of security operations
- 53:47 – Quick-fire round and closing

**Key takeaways**
- Microsoft provides the security platform, but configuring Purview, Defender and {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/microsoft-entra/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=microsoft-purview-in-the-age-of-ai-securing-copilot-with-peter-rising-microsoft|Entra}} correctly remains the customer's responsibility, ideally with an experienced partner.
- Sensitivity labels, DLP and data lifecycle management are the three Purview basics every organization should implement before rolling out Copilot.
- Copilot and Agent 365 agents are only as safe as the data and identities behind them, so tackle oversharing first and apply Zero Trust and defense in depth.

**Worth quoting** “it's true that Microsoft provides the platform and the solutions, but it's not up to Microsoft to configure that for the end users.” – Peter Rising (05:57) “zero trust has three main principles that are attached to it and that is, verify explicitly, so that ties into things like multifactor authentication” – Peter Rising (09:36) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72322206.title: The Latency Wall: Why Your Cloud Strategy Fails at the Edge
72322206.key: the latency wall why your cloud strategy fails at the edge
72322206.markup:
Cloud strategies built for dashboards and collaboration break the moment physical machines depend on millisecond decisions. This episode is for cloud architects, IT and OT leaders and Microsoft 365 professionals extending their estate to factories, ports and hospitals. Learn how Private 5G, Azure Stack Edge and edge computing move intelligence to where the work happens while staying compliant. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The physics you can't cheat
- 10:00 – Old model versus new model and the cost of backhauling
- 20:29 – What Private 5G actually does
- 26:26 – Azure Stack Edge and multi-access edge computing
- 36:20 – Event, reasoning, orchestration and the real-world return
- 47:34 – Data sovereignty and security at the edge
- 57:29 – The converged fabric and deployment patterns
- 71:22 – What this means for your cloud strategy

**Key takeaways**
- Latency is a physics problem with a hard floor, so millisecond control loops for robots, vision and vehicles must run at the edge rather than in a distant cloud region.
- Private 5G with Azure Stack Edge, Azure Arc and containerized edge workloads delivers deterministic connectivity and local intelligence while the cloud handles training, governance and analytics.
- Success depends on data quality, regulatory-grade sovereignty controls, phased rollouts and IT/OT collaboration more than on the hardware itself.

**Worth quoting** “Determinism, which is the consistency and predictability of response times, matters more than raw speed. A system that responds in five milliseconds every single time is more valuable than a system that averages three milliseconds, but occasionally spikes to 300.” – Mirko Peters (03:39) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72419835.title: Infrastructure as Code, DevOps & the Future of Azure with Maik van der Gaag [MVP]
72419835.key: infrastructure as code devops the future of azure with maik van der gaag mvp
72419835.markup:
Spinning up resources in Azure takes minutes, but doing it securely and repeatably is hard. Azure MVP Maik van der Gaag explains infrastructure as code, Bicep versus Terraform, DevOps culture and how to use AI-generated code safely, for cloud engineers and platform teams. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Introduction and Maik's path into IT
- 05:49 – Lessons from running communities
- 07:34 – Cloud trends: hybrid and sovereign cloud
- 10:12 – Cloud transformation mistakes and AI hype
- 15:25 – Infrastructure as code explained
- 21:49 – Bicep vs. Terraform, secrets and identities
- 31:51 – DevOps culture, GitOps and GitHub vs. {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-devops/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=infrastructure-as-code-devops-the-future-of-azure-with-maik-van-der-gaag-mvp|Azure DevOps}}
- 38:08 – AI for infrastructure teams and getting started

**Key takeaways**
- Infrastructure as code makes deployments repeatable, reduces typos and helps detect configuration drift compared with manual changes in the Azure portal.
- Bicep is the simpler Azure-focused choice while Terraform adds multi-cloud reach and state management, so the right tool depends on the team's scenarios and learning curve.
- AI can write much of the infrastructure code, but engineers must validate and be able to explain every line before it is deployed.

**Worth quoting** “I always see it as a piece of code or a piece of writing depending on the language you use. That represents your infrastructure.” – Maik van der Gaag (15:37) “if we specify that in a piece of infrastructure as code, he just runs the script 10 times and he gets 10 times the same result and not 10 times a different result.” – Maik van der Gaag (16:57) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72320046.title: How to Architect Low-Cost AI Agents in the Microsoft Cloud
72320046.key: how to architect low cost ai agents in the microsoft cloud
72320046.markup:
Your Azure OpenAI and Copilot Studio bills keep climbing even when usage looks flat. This episode is for architects, platform teams and FinOps leads running AI agents in the Microsoft cloud, and it shows how to find the context, reasoning and autonomous taxes and remove them with caching, compression, routing and governance. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Three hidden taxes and the four billing layers
- 03:15 – The context tax and the reasoning tax
- 09:03 – The autonomous tax and the November 2026 credit cliff
- 11:40 – Auditing spend: Cost Management, consumption estimator and token flow maps
- 21:10 – Four levers: semantic caching, LLMLingua compression, model routing, PTU vs PAYG
- 36:57 – Guardrails, the 90-day roadmap and the governance model
- 61:48 – Case study: rebuilding the Contoso support agent
- 71:00 – Advanced scenarios, emergency brakes and the weekly checklist

**Key takeaways**
- Most AI agent cost comes from architecture, not model pricing: bloated retrieval context, sending every request to the flagship model, and autonomous agents consuming {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/copilot-credits/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=how-to-architect-low-cost-ai-agents-in-the-microsoft-cloud|Copilot credits}} unchecked.
- Four levers compound when applied together: semantic caching in Azure API Management, prompt compression with LLMLingua, model routing in {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-ai-foundry/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=how-to-architect-low-cost-ai-agents-in-the-microsoft-cloud|Azure AI Foundry}}, and buying capacity correctly with PAYG or yearly PTU only at sustained high utilization.
- Cost control lasts only with governance: tag every resource, classify agents into gold, silver and bronze cost classes before they are built, and enforce budgets, credit caps and rate limits automatically.

**Explore more on M365.FM**

In this episode, Business Applications MVP Nathan Rose explains to makers, architects and consultants how Copilot Studio, Dataverse, the Dataverse MCP server and business skills fit together, and how to prepare for an agentic future. **In this episode**

- 24:00 – Dataverse business skills explained
- 27:45 – MCP explained: Spotify vs. the DJ
- 46:17 – Change management, shadow AI and what to learn next

**Worth quoting** “the way I like to frame it is, an API is like Spotify. And mcp is like a DJ. Now you've probably never thought about why do we pay DJs when we just have Spotify to play music?” – Nathan Rose (27:43) “so dataverse, what makes it so exciting is it is this common data layer in an organization.” – Nathan Rose (21:36) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72319450.title: The SLM Revolution: How Small Models Are Fixing Copilot’s Biggest Flaw
72319450.key: the slm revolution how small models are fixing copilot s biggest flaw
72319450.markup:
Copilot's real cost isn't the license but the frontier model behind every request, which drives up spend, slows responses and can process data outside the EU. This episode shows IT leaders and architects how small language models, tiered routing and local deployment on Azure Local make Copilot cheaper, faster and more sovereign. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – The broken assumption: bigger is better
- 03:17 – Cost, latency and the sovereignty gap
- 16:27 – What an SLM really is and the Phi-3 family
- 25:00 – Benchmarks, cost and latency numbers
- 32:53 – Tiered architecture and the orchestration layer
- 40:47 – Azure Local, the EU Data Boundary and M365 local AI
- 53:17 – Real-world deployments and security architecture
- 62:30 – Model mixture strategy, roadmap and ROI

**Key takeaways**
- Routing every {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/copilot/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-slm-revolution-how-small-models-are-fixing-copilots-biggest-flaw|Copilot}} request through a frontier model makes AI costly, slow and dependent on cloud processing locations you may not control.
- Small language models such as Phi-3 handle the high-volume, narrow Microsoft 365 tasks like summarization, classification and drafting at a fraction of the cost and latency.
- A tiered model mixture with policy and confidence-based routing, local deployment on Azure Local and clear governance lets organizations keep frontier models for the exceptions that need them.

**Worth quoting** “Latency isn't just a user experience problem. It's an adoption problem. If your employees try co-pilot twice, wait two seconds each time and decide it's faster to just do the work themselves, they won't come back.” – Mirko Peters (09:13) “the sovereignty conversation can't end with Microsoft says it's compliant. It has to extend to can we verify and enforce compliance ourselves.” – Mirko Peters (15:17) **Explore more on M365.FM**

72365940.title: Mastering ALM for Power Platform: From Citizen Development to Enterprise Delivery with Parvez Ghumra [MVP]
72365940.key: mastering alm for power platform from citizen development to enterprise delivery with parvez ghumra mvp
72365940.markup: What separates successful {{link|https://www.m365.fm/categories/power-platform-talk/|https://www.m365.fm/categories/power-platform-talk/}} implementations from those that become difficult to manage, impossible to scale, and increasingly risky to maintain?In this in-depth episode of the M365 Podcast, host Mirko Peters welcomes Microsoft MVP Parvez Ghumra for a comprehensive discussion on Application Lifecycle Management (ALM), enterprise delivery, governance, DevOps, CI/CD, and the future of Microsoft Power Platform development. With more than a decade of experience helping organizations implement enterprise-grade Power Platform, Dynamics 365, and Azure solutions, Parvez shares practical lessons learned from real-world projects spanning government organizations, universities, enterprises, and global businesses.As Microsoft continues to position Power Platform as the leading low-code platform for digital transformation, organizations face a growing challenge: how do you empower citizen developers while maintaining the governance, security, quality, and operational standards required by enterprise environments? {{link|https://www.m365.fm/mastering-alm-for-power-platform-from-citizen-development-to-enterprise-delivery-with-parvez-ghumra/|https://www.m365.fm/mastering-alm-for-power-platform-from-citizen-development-to-enterprise-delivery-with-parvez-ghumra/}} explores exactly that challenge and provides listeners with practical guidance for scaling Power Platform responsibly. THE JOURNEY FROM TRADITIONAL SOFTWARE ENGINEERING TO LOW-CODE DEVELOPMENT Before becoming one of the leading voices in Power Platform ALM, Parvez began his career in traditional software engineering. During the conversation, he shares his journey through ASP.NET development, C#, SQL Server, enterprise application architecture, and Dynamics CRM before eventually becoming a specialist in Application Lifecycle Management and enterprise Power Platform delivery.Parvez explains why traditional software engineering principles remain just as relevant today as they were twenty years ago. While low-code and no-code platforms simplify development, the underlying concepts of architecture, source control, deployment automation, testing, security, scalability, and governance have not disappeared. Instead, they have become even more important as organizations accelerate development and enable larger numbers of makers to build business solutions.Listeners will discover why understanding software engineering fundamentals can significantly improve the quality, reliability, and scalability of {{link|https://www.m365.fm/power-platform-solutions/|https://www.m365.fm/power-platform-solutions/}}. WHAT IS APPLICATION LIFECYCLE MANAGEMENT (ALM) AND WHY DOES IT MATTER? Application Lifecycle Management is often misunderstood as simply moving solutions between environments. In reality, ALM represents a complete framework for managing software from initial development through testing, deployment, governance, maintenance, and ongoing improvement.Parvez breaks down ALM into practical concepts that both technical and non-technical audiences can understand. He explains how source control, deployment pipelines, testing environments, automated releases, rollback capabilities, and governance frameworks work together to create predictable and reliable software delivery processes.The conversation explores why organizations that neglect ALM often experience: - Deployment failures - Uncontrolled solution growth - Security risks - Production outages - Poor collaboration between teams - Lack of visibility into changes - Difficult maintenance and support challenges At the same time, listeners learn how a well-designed ALM strategy creates confidence, consistency, repeatability, and quality across the entire software delivery lifecycle. UNDERSTANDING ENVIRONMENTS, SOLUTIONS, AND SOURCE CONTROL One of the most valuable sections of the episode focuses on explaining core Power Platform concepts in language that business leaders and stakeholders can understand.Parvez provides practical analogies for development environments, testing environments, and production environments, helping listeners understand why separation between these stages is critical. He also explains the true purpose of Power Platform solutions and why they are much more than simple containers for transporting customizations.The discussion covers: - Development environments - Test environments - Production environments - Managed solutions - Unmanaged solutions - Solution dependencies - Solution layering - Publishers and managed properties - Source control integration - Version management - Release management Whether you are a Power Platform maker, architect, administrator, or business sponsor, these concepts provide a foundation for building scalable and maintainable solutions. WHEN SHOULD ORGANIZATIONS IMPLEMENT ALM? Many organizations ask the same question: Should we think about ALM from day one, or can it wait until later?Parvez provides a nuanced answer based on years of consulting experience. For enterprise-scale projects supporting thousands of users, he argues that ALM should be considered non-negotiable and should be designed before development begins. For smaller initiatives and proof-of-concept projects, organizations may choose a lighter approach initially while still planning for future growth.The discussion highlights how organizations can evolve their ALM maturity over time without introducing unnecessary complexity too early.Listeners gain valuable guidance on: - ALM maturity models - Enterprise adoption strategies - Governance planning - Development team structures - Maker enablement - Scaling low-code solutions - Enterprise architecture considerations IS POWER PLATFORM READY FOR ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE DELIVERY? Despite being widely known as a low-code platform, Power Platform has evolved into a sophisticated enterprise application platform capable of supporting mission-critical business workloads.Parvez discusses how Power Platform has matured through its Dynamics CRM heritage and explains how capabilities such as Dataverse, Model-Driven Apps, enterprise integrations, Azure services, and advanced governance features make enterprise-grade delivery possible.The conversation explores how organizations are using Power Platform for: - Enterprise business applications - Process automation - Customer engagement solutions - Employee experience platforms - Data management - AI-powered business processes - Large-scale digital transformation initiatives Listeners gain a realistic perspective on both the strengths and limitations of the platform when deployed at scale. THE EVOLUTION OF CI/CD FOR POWER PLATFORM Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery have undergone significant transformation within the Power Platform ecosystem.Parvez explains how the early days of ALM required deep expertise in Azure DevOps, source control systems, and deployment tooling. He contrasts that with today's landscape, where features such as Power Platform Pipelines, Native Git Integration, GitHub Actions, and the Power Platform CLI have dramatically lowered the barrier to entry.The discussion explores: - CI/CD best practices - Deployment automation - Build pipelines - Release pipelines - Power Platform CLI - Git repositories - Automated testing - Quality gates - Build artifacts - Enterprise deployment strategies Listeners learn how modern tooling is making professional software delivery practices accessible to both makers and experienced development teams. AZURE DEVOPS VS GITHUB ACTIONS: WHICH SHOULD YOU CHOOSE? One of the most practical sections of the episode focuses on comparing Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions.Having implemented enterprise ALM solutions using both platforms, Parvez provides a balanced comparison of their strengths, weaknesses, and ideal use cases.Topics covered include: - Azure DevOps Boards - Work item management - GitHub Actions workflows - Source control strategies - Enterprise DevOps practices - Integration with Jira - Pipeline flexibility - Developer productivity - {{link|https://www.m365.fm/github-copilot-simply-explained/|https://www.m365.fm/github-copilot-simply-explained/}} integration - Future Microsoft investments As Microsoft continues to expand GitHub's capabilities and introduces AI-powered development experiences, understanding these differences becomes increasingly important for technology leaders and architects. REAL-WORLD ENTERPRISE ALM SUCCESS STORIES Parvez shares practical examples from customer projects where organizations successfully transformed manual deployment processes into modern, automated ALM solutions.These stories illustrate the measurable benefits organizations can achieve through proper implementation of: - Source control - Deployment automation - Environment management - Governance frameworks - Release pipelines - Automated quality controls - Team collaboration processes The discussion demonstrates how even organizations with limited DevOps experience can successfully adopt enterprise-grade delivery practices. GOVERNANCE IN THE AGE OF CITIZEN DEVELOPMENT As Power Platform adoption grows, governance becomes one of the most important considerations for organizations.The conversation explores how businesses can balance innovation with control while empowering makers to build solutions safely and responsibly.Parvez discusses: - Environment strategies - Securi Become a supporter of this podcast: {{link|https://www.spreaker.com/podcast/m365-fm-microsoft-365-azure-cloud-power-platform-ai--6704921/support?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss|https://www.spreaker.com/podcast/m365-fm-microsoft-365-azure-cloud-power-platform-ai--6704921/support}}.

72295566.title: The Billion-Vector Problem: HNSW vs. DiskANN in Azure AI Search
72295566.key: the billion vector problem hnsw vs diskann in azure ai search
72295566.markup:
Vector search that looks cheap at ten million embeddings can turn into a RAM budget crisis at a billion. This episode is for Azure and AI architects building RAG and enterprise search on Azure AI Search, Cosmos DB or SQL Server. You get a practical framework for choosing between HNSW and DiskANN based on scale, update frequency, latency and cost. **In this episode**
- 00:00 – Why the HNSW default becomes a budget problem
- 04:07 – Vector search and approximate nearest neighbor basics
- 07:24 – HNSW explained and the memory wall
- 13:39 – DiskANN architecture and production numbers
- 20:15 – DiskANN in Azure and the four-variable decision framework
- 27:19 – RAM vs. SSD cost model and index mutability
- 33:34 – RAG pipelines, failure modes, metadata filtering and multi-tenancy
- 54:03 – Evaluation, observability, roadmap and the decision guide

**Key takeaways**
- HNSW keeps the whole graph in RAM and is the right choice for smaller corpora with strict latency needs, but at roughly a billion vectors it needs terabytes of memory per replica.
- DiskANN keeps a compressed navigation layer in RAM and the full graph on SSD, reaching similar recall at a fraction of the memory, with {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/cosmos-db/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-billion-vector-problem-hnsw-vs-diskann-in-azure-ai-search|Cosmos DB}} suited to dynamic data and SQL Server to static data.
- Index choice drives cost, while answer quality depends on hybrid search, reranking, chunking, chunk-level metadata filters and continuous evaluation and observability.

**Worth quoting** “The main reason enterprise rag fails is retrieval, not generation. When your model gives a plausible but wrong answer, it usually isn't because the model invented a lie. It's because the right context never actually made it into the prompt.” – Mirko Peters (37:37) “The vector index itself should never surface a document the user isn't allowed to see no matter how relevant that document is to the search. Semantic similarity is a great tool for finding information but it is not an authorization mechanism.” – Mirko Peters (47:22) **Explore more on M365.FM**
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/show/episodes/the-billion-vector-problem-hnsw-vs-diskann-in-azure-ai-search/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-billion-vector-problem-hnsw-vs-diskann-in-azure-ai-search|Episode page}}: the full episode with chapters, key quotes and an FAQ on vector indexing
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/azure-ai-search/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-billion-vector-problem-hnsw-vs-diskann-in-azure-ai-search|Azure AI Search}} – the service whose HNSW indexing, hybrid search, filters and semantic ranking anchor the episode
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/rag/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-billion-vector-problem-hnsw-vs-diskann-in-azure-ai-search|Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)}} – the pipeline whose answer quality depends on retrieval, chunking, filters and evaluation, not the index
- {{link|https://www.m365.fm/entity/cosmos-db/?utm_source=podcast&utm_medium=shownotes&utm_campaign=the-billion-vector-problem-hnsw-vs-diskann-in-azure-ai-search|Azure Cosmos DB}} – the recommended DiskANN implementation for dynamic data and corpora beyond 100 million vectors
